Economics Week Ahead Economics
CPI • Friday
Headline inflation looks to have picked up last month. We estimate
the CPI rose 0.40% in August, with gasoline prices increasing a little
over 4% as renewed tensions in the Middle East pushed oil higher.
Grocery prices also likely rebounded after modestly declining in July.
Outside of food and energy, price pressures appear little changed.
We expect the core CPI to rise 0.23%, essentially matching July's

pace. Core goods inflation should remain firm, led by another solid
increase in used vehicle prices as consumer prices continue to
catch up to the trend indicated at wholesale auctions. Meantime,
household furnishings and other tariff-sensitive categories appear
to be stabilizing after declining earlier this year.
Core services inflation should be little changed with another 0.2%
monthly increase. But underneath the surface, we expect a modest
pickup in travel (led by lodging away from home) to offset slightly

cooler medical care and housing cost growth.
All told, we expect the report to show that while headline inflation
remains influenced by the ebbs and flows of the conflict in the
Middle East, core inflation remains contained. Should our forecast
prove correct, core CPI will ease to 2.4% year-over-year, in line with
its 6-month annualized rate but above the more recent 3-month
annualized pace of 1.7%.

### Page 4

Weekly Economics
G10 Week Ahead
European Central Bank Monetary Policy Meeting •
Thursday
We expect the European Central Bank (ECB) to raise the Deposit
Rate by 25 bps to 2.50% next week. August headline inflation
remained elevated at 3.3% year-over-year, though softer core
and services inflation suggest underlying pressures continue to
moderate. Still, the more hawkish tone of the July minutes and
renewed rise in energy prices should keep policymakers cautious.

The recent escalation in the Middle East has pushed fuel prices
at the pump close to their 2022 peaks, while natural gas storage
remains below historical levels, leaving the Eurozone vulnerable
to further energy price increases. The ECB is unlikely to respond
aggressively if the shock remains confined to energy given the
downside risks to growth. However, a broader rise in food inflation
linked to El Niño would be more concerning, as highly visible prices

could lift inflation expectations and generate second-round effects.
For now, resilient Q3 activity, elevated headline inflation and
contained wage growth support one final hike. The ECB will likely
retain and emphasize its scenario-based outlook in the updated
staff projections given continued uncertainty around the conflict
and energy prices. The policy path beyond September will depend
on whether energy and food pressures persist and begin to spread,

which could leave room for further tightening.

Economics Week Ahead Economics
EM Week Ahead
Mexico CPI • Wednesday
We expect Mexico’s August inflation rate to edge higher, with
headline CPI rising to 3.34% year-over-year (0.27% month-over-
month) from 3.26% year-over-year in early August. Part of the
pickup likely reflects less favorable base effects and a smaller
disinflationary contribution from food prices. While agricultural
prices continued to help restrain inflation in mid-August, the drag

was notably less pronounced than in July. Core inflation should
remain elevated at 3.98% year-over-year (0.25% month-over-
month).
While inflation remains within Banxico’s midpoint 3% target,
persistent core and services inflation suggest convergence toward
the midpoint of the target could prove gradual. For now, we
continue to expect Banxico to keep rates on hold, with the policy
rate remaining at 6.50% through the rest of 2026 and into early
2027 as policymakers await clearer evidence that underlying

inflation pressures are easing sustainably. While rate cuts remain
a possibility in 2027, the current inflation backdrop argues for
patience in the near term.

Brazil CPI • Friday
We expect Brazil’s August inflation rate to slow to 4.20% year-over-
year, helped by lower electricity, food and fuel prices. The main
driver should be a temporary reduction in residential electricity bills
stemming from a one-off credit, while recent data already point to
a notable easing in price pressures. Mid-August CPI came in weaker
than expected, with inflation falling to 4.24% year-over-year amid
declines in electricity, food, fuel and airfare prices. Beyond these

temporary factors, restrictive monetary policy continues to weigh
on economic activity, as evidenced by the recent slowdown in Q2
GDP growth. However, underlying inflation risks remain. A still-
tight labor market and government measures aimed at supporting
consumption could keep services inflation sticky, making progress
toward the 3.0% inflation target more gradual.
Overall, the inflation outlook remains consistent with additional
policy easing. We expect COPOM to deliver a 25 bps rate cut in

September, bringing the Selic Rate to 13.75%. Beyond September,
policymakers are likely to proceed cautiously as they assess
incoming inflation data and the impact of the election cycle on
inflation expectations. Our base case remains for a pause after
September, with additional easing more likely in 2027.

Document 1280: Fed builds credibility with hike; one more likely in Dec

### Page 1

Fed builds credibility with 
hike; one more likely in Dec 
Summary 
Event: The US Federal Reserve hiked its key interest rate by 
25bps to 3.75-4.0%, in a unanimous decision. This marks the 
first hike since 2023, reversing the easing cycle that had 
taken rates down from 4.25% in September 2025 to a trough 
of 3.75% by December 2025. The revised projections 
indicate the Fed expects to raise rates by an additional 25bps 
this year, hold rates in 2027, and cut 25bps in both 2028 and 
2029. It upgraded the long-run rate slightly to 3.2%.  
Market reaction: The US yield curve mildly flattened , while 
the S&P500 index fell 0.5%. The policy rate sensitive US 2 -
year government bond yield jumped 7 bps to 4. 74% as 
markets factored in  three more 25bps hikes by June 2027 . 
The US 10-year yield rose 2bps to 5.02%, its highest since 
2007, while the 30-year yield was little changed. The USD 
index (DXY) rose 0.6%, breaking past its 50- and 100-DMAs. 
Investment strategy: Today’s move realises what we had 
been flagging in recent weeks i.e. the rising risk of a Fed rate 
hike following Fed Chair Warsh’s Jackson Hole speech and 
recent economic data prints, namely: a pick-up in job creation 
and inflation over the summer and a sharp rebound in oil 
prices due to the re-escalation of the Middle East conflict.  
This hike helps the Fed rebuild credibility as an inflation 
fighter. Given the unanimous decision to hike rates this week, 
we believe there will likely be one more hike before the end 
of this year, and one more in H1 2027 as we expect robust 
growth amid strong AI investments and a tight labour market, 
keeping inflation elevated.  That scenario would still be less 
than the three more rate hikes money markets are pricing 
after the latest Fed move. We believe policy rates can return 
to the 4.0 –4.25% range by end-2027, with the possibility of 
cuts in H2 2027  as the impact of tariffs and high oil prices 
start to fade towards the second half of 2027.   
Today’s refreshed Fed policy rate path is mildly bullish for the 
USD index; so we revise up our 3 -month target to 100. We 
also revise up our 3-month 10-year yield target to 5.0-5.25%.  
 The USD rose, while stocks fell after the Fed hiked rates 
and signalled one more rate hike this year; ultra-long 
bonds rose slightly as the Fed rebuild its inflation-
fighting credentials

Backdrop to the rate hike 
In hiking rates, Fed Chair Warsh reaffirmed the inflation 
threat to the US economy. US headline inflation accelerated 
to 0.4% m/m in August and stayed elevated on an annualised 
basis at 3.4% y/y. Energy prices , driven by the Middle East 
conflict, were a primary contributor. Oil prices have extended 
gains since the August inflation report, surging past USD 
100/bbl. Meanwhile, core inflation rose 0.3% m/m in August, 
beating estimates for a 0.2% rise . Also, US producer prices 
jumped 0.4% m/m in August, the most since May, and 5.4%  
y/y, further reinforcing the inflationary backdrop. 
The inflation report follow ed a stronger -than-expected jobs 
report for August. US monthly job creation has surged to an 
average 80,000 this year, from 10,000, tightening a job 
market that already faces a supply crunch from the Trump 
administration’s clampdown against immigration.  The 
combination of an acceleration in job creation and inflation 
over the summer, combined with a rebound in oil prices, 
supported our expectation for a Fed rate hike this week.  
Removing “a dose of accommodation” 
Warsh framed the decision to hike as removing "a dose of 
accommodation", rather than the start of an aggressive rate 
hiking cycle, and we agree with that characterisation. The aim 
is to bring financial and credit conditions more in line with the 
Fed's price stability objectives. To quote Warsh: “Our 
predominant focus is on the price stability side of our 
mandate. The plain fact is that inflation is too high, and has 
been for too long….This  summer’s inflation readings do not 
tell me that underlying trends have meaningfully improved.” 
He added that many categories in the last consumer and 
producer inflation reports are still showing price increases 
above 3% on a six- and 12-month basis.  
The unanimous vote to hike rates, contrasts with a 9 -3 split 
vote in July to hold rates. When combined with the pencilling 
in of one more hike by December, this suggests a majority of 
Fed policymakers have turned more hawkish over the 
summer. In doing so, they have helped rebuild the Fed’s 
inflation-fighting credentials and its independence against 
President Trump’s pressures to cut rates. This explains why 
long-end bond yields were stable after this week’s hike. 
Nevertheless, Warsh provided little guidance on the future 
rate path, as he held what was reportedly the shortest post -
meeting press conference on record for a Fed chair . This is 
consistent with his stated preference for less central bank 
communication. We expect more clarity once the Fed task 
forces submit their reports by year end. 
— Jonathan Liang, CIO for Fixed Income and FX   
Rajat Bhattacharya, Senior Investment Strategist

0:00:10 - Emmanuel Laborde 
Everyone, welcome. As we head into autumn 2026, interest rates are reaching levels never seen for many, many years. 
Why is this happening? Is it sustainable? And what are the implications for the economies of different countries? All these 
questions will be discussed over the next few minutes with the economists of BNP Paribas. Let us begin with Isabelle 
Mateos y Lago, chief economist of the group. Hello, Isabelle.

Hello Emmanuel, hello everyone. 
0:00:39 - Emmanuel Laborde 
Thank you for being with us today. Just to begin, a simple explanation. What rates are we talking about and which countries

0:00:48 - Isabelle Mateos y Lago 
Yes, it is very important to clarify this. So, we are talking about long-term interest rates, rates at 10 years or longer 
maturities, 30 years, etc. The rates at which sovereign states borrow on the market. And this is primarily something that is 
happening in advanced countries, so United States, United King dom, Japan, and then the Eurozone countries. And indeed, 
as you said, we are seeing since the beginning of the summer, interest rates reach levels we had not seen for about 20 
years. But it is important to keep in mind that up until that point, up until the mid -2000s, the level of interest rates that 
we're seeing now were really quite common, quite normal, so one shouldn't overdramatize.  
0:01:35 - Emmanuel Laborde 
Why do we find ourselves in this situation and how did we get to this point?  
0:01:41 - Isabelle Mateos y Lago 
Yes, so the direct cause is that investors are demanding higher interest rates in order to  lend their capital to governments. 
But why is this? Well, there's essentially three reasons for this, and not all of them are bad, and they're not mutually 
exclusive either. The top reason to my mind is that there's just greater competition for capital be tween sovereign states 
and the corporate sector, who are all facing simultaneously additional investment needs, in defense, in artificial 
intelligence, in energy transition, in resilience. And so,  you just have greater competition for capital and that pushes up the 
price of capital, which is the interest rate. 
Reason number two is because markets have revised upwards their expectations of how high central banks are going to be 
taking their interest rates. 
And this mechanically translates into higher rates at the long end. And then there's a third reason, which doesn't apply 
necessarily in every case, but which is essentially higher sovereign risk, a kind of a risk premium, in cases where there are  
concerns arising about the sustainability of these public debts.

WESTPAC ECONOMICS
TODAY’S INSIGHTS
Financial Markets
Markets were generally buoyed overnight, with Anthropic’s
IPO filing and Meta’s US$25bn equity offering closing five
times oversubscribed adding momentum back into the
AI trade, while softer oil prices provided further support.

Attention now turns to a series of key economic developments,
with Australian CPI due today alongside policy decisions and
accompanying guidance from the RBNZ, BoC and FOMC.
• US equities moved higher, supported by AI-related
stocks. The S&P 500 gained 0.8%, while the NASDAQ
outperformed, rising 1.2%, and the Dow Jones was
unchanged. European markets were mixed, with the Euro
Stoxx 50 up 0.8%, while the FTSE 100 fell 0.8% ahead of
the UK Budget.
• Tech-heavy Asian markets were buoyed as recent headlines

helped ease concerns around AI financing. The KOSPI led
gains, rising 3.1%, while the Nikkei 225 also performed
strongly, up 1.7%. The Hang Seng diverged from regional
peers, falling 0.7%. Locally, the ASX 200 gained 0.5%.
• US Treasury yields were little changed, with the 2-year
yield rising 1bp and the 10-year yield unchanged. Futures
markets remain cautious about pricing further Fed tightening
in 2026, with the probability of a hike at today’s FOMC

meeting sitting at just 7%, taking the implied year-end fed
funds rate to 4.10%.
• Australian government bond yields were little changed
ahead of today’s CPI release, with the 3-year yield rising
1bp and the 10-year yield falling 1bp. Swap markets remain
cautious around additional RBA tightening in 2026, with the
probability of a November rate hike priced at 62%, taking
the implied year-end cash rate to 4.80%.
• Pre-FOMC positioning supported the US dollar, with

the DXY up 0.3%. The AUD outperformed other major
currencies, rising 0.2% against the greenback to 0.7028 and
also gaining across the major crosses. The euro and yen both
fell 0.3% against the USD, while the sterling declined 0.2%.
• Oil prices declined on hopes that diplomacy could avert a
renewed escalation in the US-Iran conflict. Brent fell 1.6%
to US$114/bbl, while WTI declined 1.9% to US$99.9/bbl.
Dated Brent traded at US$121/bbl. Gold rose 1.1% ahead

of today’s FOMC meeting, while positive risk sentiment
supported base metals, with copper up 1.0% and aluminium
gaining 1.5%. Iron ore fell 1.1%, remaining below US$90/t
amid persistent concerns around global demand.
International Data
US durable goods orders rose 1.8% in September after a 0.1%
gain in August. Growth for core orders (non defence, ex aircraft)
was more modest in September at 0.5% but follows a 1.6% rise
in August.
US S&P Cotality Case Shiller house prices rose a further 0.3%

in August, accelerating annual growth at the margin to 2.7%yr.
US new home sales fell 0.6% in September following a
downwardly revised 5.1% gain (prev 6.4%) in August. Sales are
currently near the average of the past 5 years.
US Conference Board consumer confidence jumped from 84.2
to 91.7 in October on an improvement in current conditions
and expectations. While still below average, this measure of
consumer confidence continues to outperform the University of

Michigan survey, held up by the robust strength of the labour
market. Responses to the Michigan measure instead look to be
focused more on cost of living.
The Richmond Fed manufacturing index was unchanged at -2
in October.
Local Data
Our New Zealand team published their 2026 General Election
preview, outlining the major parties’ key policies (see here).

Document 1336: Q3 Growth in advanced economies_ solid despite shocks (2026-10-23)

Source PDF: all report pdf/Q3 Growth in advanced economies_ solid despite shocks (2026-10-23).pdf
Report source: BNP Paribas
Date: 2026-10-23
Pages: 2
Status: ok

### Page 1

Paris, 23 October 2026

EcoFlash

Q3 Growth in advanced economies: solid despite shocks

Growth looks to have held up in Q3 despite successive shocks (see our analysis), as it did in 2025 and H1 2026. A longer 
Middle East conflict has fed into more persistent inflation; drought has worsened in many countries, and interest rates 
have risen further – at the short end, with both the ECB and the Fed raising policy rates in September, and even more at 
the long end. However, our nowcasts show that growth is bending without breaking in most advanced economies. GDP 
figures (due on 29 October in the US and 30 October for the euro area and its member states) are expected to confirm 
that. In the Euro area, momentum looks stable (excluding Ireland, whose GDP is volatile). In Germany, growth has been 
uninterrupted since Q4 2025, while France is likely to have returned to growth after stagnating in H1. In the US, growth 
is likely to have gathered pace, according to the GDP Now, still driven by AI, but increasingly by other sectors as well.

Euro area: resilience beneath the surface. Our nowcast points to growth slowing to 0.3% in q/q, though the pace is stable 
excluding Ireland (Irish GDP is volatile and had markedly boosted the Q2 figure). Excluding Ireland, growth should hold at its H2 
average, a sign of the bloc’s underlying resilience. Also, momentum has broadened to a growing number of sectors ( see our 
analysis). While industrial production stalled over the summer, services remained buoyant. The services PMI rebounded sharply 
in Q3 and sits firmly in expansion territory (53.0 in September). Improving job-related survey data (PMI and European Commission 
surveys) and a stable unemployment rate (6.4% in August) hint at more hiring in Q3 – a support for household consumption that 
partly offsets purchasing-power losses from persistent inflation. Corporate investment is underpinned by buoyant new investment 
lending (8.7% y/y In August, 12-month cumulative). 
France: growing, nevertheless. The succession of shocks does not appear to have prevented France from returning to 
growth in Q3, at 0.2% q/q, according to our nowcast. One-off factors accounted for the stall in activity in H1. In Q3, the drought 
worsened and industrial production remained subdued. However, market services production rebounded in July and August, 
notably in business services, restaurants, digital and real estate. The latter points to residential investment recovering after a weak 
H1. Corporate investment likely followed, as reflected in buoyant credit flows and AI-related investment. Household consumption 
is likely to have improved slightly on higher electric vehicle sales.  
Euro area  France

Source: Refinitiv, BNP Paribas  Source: Refinitiv, BNP Paribas

Germany: growth still solid. The H1 rebound in activity is moderating but continues. Our nowcast points to a fourth straight 
quarter of growth in Q3, at 0.2% q/q (after 0.3% in Q4 2025, 0.4% in Q1 2026, and 0.3% in Q2). Manufacturing activity eased 
slightly, according to the September PMI survey (53.9, down 0.4 m/m). Government spending will remain growth-supportive, with 
defence and infrastructure outlays gaining traction. Infrastructure spending continues to underpin activity in public works, which 
stands at its highest since November 2021 (2.5% 3m/3m in August). Exports (4.4% y/y between January and August) remain the 
main growth engine, helped by a pivot towards Europe (7.2%). 
United States: an expansion undeterred by inflation. Growth is likely to have gathered pace in Q3. The Atlanta Fed’s GDP 
Now points to a 3.5% annualized growth rate (AR), close to our own 3.7% forecast (0.9% non -AR) and up from 2.2% in 
Q2. Domestic demand remains the engine. Consumption is weathering the pickup in inflation, while the AI-driven capex cycle 
remains robust – as reflected in retail sales and nondefence capital-goods orders (excl. aircraft). As a result, growth in final sales

### Page 2

to private domestic purchasers 1 should print above 4% AR again. By contrast, external trade should remain a drag on growth, 
reflecting AI-related import needs. Survey data point to mome ntum that is both solid and broad -based. The ISM indices have 
remained firmly in growth territory (54.9 quarterly average for manufacturing and services alike). At the same time, they highlight 
persistent price and supply-chain pressures.

Germany   United States

• The Westpac–DataX Card Tracker
Index* has edged down slightly since
late September, slipping 0.9pts to 160.6
in the week ended October 17. Despite
this, growth in activity continues to track
a robust pace with quarterly momentum

running at close to 2%qtr and annual
growth at 6%yr.
• Some of this reflects revisions. Initial
figures on card activity can see changes
in subsequent weeks due to information
lags. While these are usually small,
the cumulative impact can sometimes
be material. In this case, revisions have
lifted the index in late September by
2.5pts and the 4wk trend growth rate at
the time from 0.2% to 0.6%. We will be
back-testing regular revisions to assess
whether there is a systematic bias that

can be adjusted for in future.
• The revised profile shows quarterly
growth accelerating steadily since
June, posting a 1.9%qtr gain for the
September quarter and tracking a
2.1%qtr pace in the latest week. This is
back near the robust pace seen in late
2024 and early 2025.
• The monthly and weekly reads show
a softer 0.2%mth rise in August was
followed by a solid 0.8%mth gain in
September that has largely carried into
the first two weeks of October (the latest

observation tracking a 0.4%mth pace).
• The detail shows gains are not just
due to higher fuel prices with strong
growth in discretionary services and
international transactions over the last
quarter and steady growth in essential
services as well. To the extent that the
weekly and monthly data is showing
some renewed squeeze from higher fuel
prices, this is showing through most
clearly in discretionary goods, which
have seen activity decline over the last

six weeks, with discretionary services
still posting positive, albeit slower
growth. Quarterly growth in non-fuel
card activity is tracking around 1.4%qtr.
• Official September quarter figures on
inflation and household spending due
in the coming weeks should confirm the
spending momentum and shed more
light on the extent to which it is due to
prices or volumes.

the forecasts may be affected by incorrect assumptions or by known or unknown risks and uncertainties. The results ultimately achieved may differ substantially from these forecasts.
WESTPAC ECONOMICS 6
• The Westpac Card Tracker draws on
a rich dataset that sheds light on many
aspects of consumer demand. In some
cases, it can also reveal some nuances
about the way spend is captured – in
official statistics, industry measures and
the card data itself. Vehicles provide a

particularly good example of this.
• Vehicle spend has long been a
bellwether for the wider consumer cycle.
As a large discretionary expenditure, it is
more sensitive to interest rate changes,
‘wealth effects’ and sentiment shifts,
particularly around job security. Given
this, ABS measures and industry figures
on vehicle sales have delivered material
upside surprises over the last year.
Vehicle purchases recorded a remarkable
10.3%qtr surge in the June quarter to be

up 7.3%yr with industry figures showing
vehicle sales holding around these levels
in the September quarter. Even allowing
‘extenuating circumstances’ driving
strong demand for EVs, the results seem
to fly in the face of wider interest rate,
cost-of-living and sentiment narratives.
• The card tracker data allows for a deeper
dive. Note that credit and debit cards are
not often used to purchase vehicles with
account transfers or financing typically

used for the main purchase instead.
• However, cards are used for up-front
payments. This shows through in
payment sizes, which are in the hundreds
of dollars (average $750) not the tens of
thousands. As such, card activity should
still give some guide, particularly around
sales volumes.
• Chart 8 shows how transactions have
tracked and highlight another important
point. Most of the data in this space
focuses on new vehicles (for the ABS
this is because used sales are a transfer

between households that ‘cancels out’ for
the sector as a whole). However, industry
estimates show used sales are both more
common and have been tracking a weaker
profile – the card data suggests used sales
are down at least 3%yr (finer estimates
putting the figure closer to 8%yr).
• Age-groups offer another insightful lens.
Activity has been much firmer across
older age groups, particularly in the ‘new
vehicle’ segment where they are more
prominent (accounting for 42% of all

activity) and activity is up on a year ago.
This group has notably stronger balance
sheets and is low exposure to interest
rate rises. In contrast, vehicle spend has
been contracting materially across other
age-groups, particularly used car spend
by the ‘mortgage belt’ 35-54 year olds.

WESTPAC ECONOMICS 10
About the Westpac card data indicators
The indicators presented in this report are based on the millions of credit and debit card
transactions processed every day. Transactions covering over ten million merchants are
classified into over 700 categories. These are in turn grouped into higher level aggregates

that provide a timely guide to wider economic trends.
The main focus of these indicators is consumer spending. Where possible, we have sought
to exclude ‘non spending’ transactions such as: money transfers; tax payments; loan
repayments; charitable donations; and superannuation contributions.
It should also be noted that these indicators will also be affected by shifts between card and
non-card transactions. This was a significant factor during the COVID–19 pandemic – health

concerns about the use of physical cash leading to significantly higher use of cards vs cash,
particularly where contact–less transactions are available. Transaction flows also include
reversals/refunds which were also a significant phenomenon during the onset of COVID,
especially in areas such as travel.
All transaction data is compiled at a highly aggregated level so that individual customer or
merchant data is never revealed.
Index construction

The key metrics used in this report are indexes of spending–related card activity where the
base of 100 is average activity in 2019. As an example, if transaction flows are 5% above their
average level in 2019, the index read for the period is 105. If flows in a subsequent period are
8% above the average level in 2019, the index read for this period is 108. Growth between the
two periods can be calculated simply as the change between the two index reads, i.e. 2.9%.

All measures are adjusted for regular seasonality. Weekly estimates are generated using
the US Bureau of Labor’s MoveReg weekly seasonal adjustment program. Note that in some
cases, high levels of volatility during the COVID period mean it is not possible to produce
seasonally adjusted estimates for some historical periods.
Also, note that previous versions of this report used different approaches to seasonal
adjustment and measurement more generally. This means Index reads are sometimes not

directly comparable. See the ‘About the Westpac card data indicators’ sections from earlier
reports to more detail.
Classifications
Note that the measures used for card data and in this report do not align completely with
the those used in official ABS statistics, including the ABS household spending indicator,
ABS retail trade survey and ABS estimate of consumer spending published in the national
accounts. There are a range of differences including around both coverage and classification.

As such, the card data should be treated as broadly indicative.
The transaction data is grouped into 26 categories that are then combined into four main as
follows:
Discretionary goods: alcoholic beverages, tobacco, clothing & footwear, furnishings &
household equipment, household appliances, vehicle–related, recreational & cultural goods,
newspaper, books & stationery, and other personal effects.
Discretionary services: transport services (part), recreational & cultural services, gambling,

catering services, accommodation services, other personal care, insurance & financial
services, other services.
Essential goods: food & non alcoholic beverages, medical products, appliances & equipment,
and operation of personal transport equipment.
Essential services: electricity, gas & other fuels, health services, transport services (part),
communications and education.
The report also uses two additional classifications:
MHSI/Retail: based on the extent to which categories cover activity that is in scope for the

ABS monthly household spending indicator and ABS retail trade survey.

Document 1394: What’s the Renminbi Got to Do With it_ (2026-10-11)

Source PDF: all report pdf/What’s the Renminbi Got to Do With it_ (2026-10-11).pdf
Report source: CFR (Follow the Money)
Date: 2026-10-11
Pages: 17
Status: ok

### Page 1

1
EXPERT TAKE FOLLOW THE MONEY
What’s the Renminbi Got to Do With it?
A closer look at the impact of China’s currency on China’s export growth.
Sean Yong/Reuters
UPDATED
October 11, 2026 12:00 a.m.
Articles Follow the Money Share
Log In
Regions Topics Research Experts Events The Future of American Strategy

### Page 2

2
Brad W. Setser CFR EXPERT
Whitney Shepardson Senior Fellow
There is an argument—made in the recent Geneva
Report and by various former IMF officials—that
China’s current export surge is the simple
consequence of the housing downturn and the
resulting weakness in Chinese internal demand.*
The weakness in the RMB in this story is entirely
incidental to the increase in exports, which is, more or
less, a mechanical response to weak internal demand.

Cannot sell excavators at home? Export them.
Built more modern car capacity than your internal
market supports? Export that too…
The fall in the nominal RMB over the course of 2022
and the first half of 2023 in nominal and read terms
was simply a function of domestic macroeconomic
weakness, and a growing rate differential. It wasn’t an
active policy choice by China’s central bank.

### Page 3

3
Now, some might note that China’s currency doesn’t
always move with rate differentials. The RMB didn’t
consistently get pulled up when Chinese rates were
higher than U.S. rates (2002-2020 generally
speaking), and while it did fall when rate differentials
moved against the RMB in 2022 and 2023, it then
stabilized and has even appreciated modestly since
the middle of last year. That appreciation hasn’t been
big enough to correct the deep undervaluation of the

RMB, but it came at a time when the PBOC policy
rate (the reverse repo rate) was well below the U.S.
policy rate.
China doesn’t have an open financial account. As a
result, equilibrium in the foreign exchange market is
thus driven far more by exporter conversion and
current account flows than by rate differentials and
financial flows.** That, together with China’s ongoing
management of the exchange rate and a trade surplus
that can generate significant inflows, means that the

### Page 4

4
value of the RMB is much more of a policy variable
under the independent control of the Chinese
authorities than a simple byproduct of monetary and
fiscal policies.
The modern IMF is reluctant to accept this
conclusion. Its surveillance has generally ignored
China’s currency management (even if that
management is relatively obvious; see the data on FX
settlement) and its recent comprehensive assessment
of China’s economy completely ignored the balance of

payments and exchange rate management.
But it is pretty obvious to the market, even if the
PBOC, rather absurdly, insists that “market forces
play a decisive role in determining the RMB
exchange rate.”
I doubt the PBOC can win this argument. I agree
with Mark Sobel:
“The renminbi is still heavily managed and the
authorities have acted to slow appreciation. The paper
states that the PBoC phased out ‘regular’ foreign
exchange intervention in 2017. But it has many

means at its disposal to achieve the same effect
through extensive capital controls, administrative
guidance, signalling at the fix and deploying state-
owned commercial banks. These means are heavily
used. Thus, the word ‘regular’ must be taken with a
pinch of salt. The comparison to Japan, which

### Page 5

5
intervenes occasionally, is spurious – the yen largely
floats freely in integrated global markets. The same
cannot be said for the renminbi.”
In reality, the PBOC’s daily fix now plays the decisive
role in the currency’s path, and the market is often a
bet on how the PBOC’s management of the yuan will
evolve.
That is clear from the lack of volatility in the yuan’s
rate against the dollar. The yuan’s move down against
the dollar in 2022 was a controlled 10 percent move,

and the appreciation over the last 16 months has been
even more controlled crawl.
And the market is clearly massaged with substantial
help from the state banks. In fact that the pattern of
changes in the monthly FX settlement data looks
exactly like the pattern of intervention of a central
bank managing its currency around a tight band (the

### Page 6

6
state banks in practice buy FX to keep the CNY from
testing the strong side of the band, so there is an
asymmetry in how the CNY is managed)
None of this would matter much if China’s economy
was small. But that obviously isn’t the case. Nor would
this matter much if China’s exports didn’t respond to
changes in the RMB’s real (and nominal) value. But
that is also not the case.
There is abundant evidence that China’s exports do
respond to moves in the currency. Periods of RMB

weakness have consistently been associated with
periods of especially rapid Chinese export growth.

### Page 7

7
Chancellor Merz and President Macron got this
right, even if macroeconomic issues haven’t yet
figured prominently in the EU’s dialogue with
China.*** As they note in their open letter to the
European Commission:
“An appreciation of undervalued currencies towards a value
more in line with fundamentals would help support the
rebalancing of trade accounts with the EU in the short and
medium term … European policy discussions focused on
forging a common understanding of these exchange rate issues

and their interaction with global imbalances would be useful.”
The best evidence that exports responded to changes
in the currency, and not simply to changes in the path
of China’s internal demand, is the acceleration in
China’s export growth after the RMB’s depreciation
over the course of 2022.
This is the killer chart.

### Page 8

8
Now, you might ask: what of the acceleration in
export growth in 2020 and 2021? That was pretty
clearly tied to the global increase in goods demand
that came with the pandemic and work from home
requirements. It was expected to fade when the world
economy normalized. But it didn’t. By 2023 Chinese
export growth again topped global trade growth.
The general expectation that the rise in China’s goods
surplus during Covid would prove to be “transitory”

### Page 9

9
heavily influenced the IMF’s work at the time: see the
IMF’s external sector reports of 2023 and 2024.
I would argue that neglecting the exchange rate was
the key reason the IMF’s kept forecasting, incorrectly,
that China’s current account surplus would fall (See
this blog with Shahin Vallee). The IMF certainly
didn’t warn that China’s property downturn and the
RMB’s real depreciation risked a second China shock
in its 2022, 2023, or 2024 surveillance reports.

Concretely, the weaker RMB appears to have
contributed to a very large outperformance of China’s
exports relative to global trade. See the following
chart
That incidentally also happened after the RMB
followed the dollar down in 2003.
In both periods, there were significant structural
shifts. The WTO accession in 2002, and the success

### Page 10

10
of Chinese industrial policies in the “green” industrial
sectors and autos in 2022. In both cses exports were
turbocharged when structural shifts that should have
resulted in a stronger currency were instead amplified
by currency weakness.
No matter. Paul Krugman has noted that a country
that is converging technologically with its trade
partners should see a trend appreciation in its
currency. China got the technological convergence,
but not the real appreciation—at least not until this

year. And the move since the middle of 2025 has
corrected the depreciation of the RMB that occurred
when the RMB followed the dollar down on
liberation day, but not the structural overvaluation.
Now, there is an argument that exchange rate
adjustment is too hot an issue to make it a priority.
The PBOC isn’t interested it seems.
And some believe that in the interest of comity and
good relations with China, the IMF should mirror
the PBOC’s views. After all a stronger RMB would

slow China’s exports and thus slow China’s economy
at a time when China needs export growth to escape
deflation and generate employment. Or so the
argument goes. Concerns about “external balance“
and the negative global spillovers from China’s rising
goods surplus should be ignored and the Fund’s sole
focus should be on policies that lead to internal

### Page 11

11
balance. That provides one rationale for the Fund’s
ongoing decision to essentially ignore the contentious
issue of the PBOC’s ongoing exchange rate
management.
That argument, however, assumes that China’s
economy is small and thus China’s external surplus
can safely be ignored because it isn’t a drag on the
growth of the IMF’s other members.
That clearly isn’t true.
And it isn’t clear that China is more interested in
having a negotiation over its level of basic pension

benefits or the size of its fiscal deficit (where the
IMF continues to make timid recommendations that
would not move the needle—and certainly wouldn’t
meaningfully reduce China’s external surplus) than a
discussion over its currency practices.****
Back in the world of fixed but adjustable exchange
rates, there was an expectation (not always met to be
sure) that surplus countries would allow their
currencies to strengthen to bring their economies

back into external balance, and that other policy tools
would be used to ensure internal balance.
I would argue that China’s exchange rate (against
both the dollar and the basket) has many similarities
to the old world of fixed but adjustable currencies.
True, it moves on a controlled path when it moves

### Page 12

12
between different levels rather than jumping up and
down. But the PBOC does frequently target a level,
and that targeted level does change over time.
I would further argue that steps like the recent tariff
rate quota that will limit China’s exports of hybrid
cars to Europe to around 350,000 units next year (up
from 2025, but well below the 800,000 units of
2026) aren’t going to address the underlying
imbalance on their own. They can provide a bit of a

buffer for specific sectors.
But that buffer, while necessary, won’t address the
broad-based erosion of manufacturing capacity
outside China. This erosion will persist as long as an
undervalued RMB sends the entire world a signal to
use China as its production base.
The new system of managed trade that is emerging in
autos would need to be progressively expanded to an
ever-increasing set of sectors if protection is used as a
substitute for both domestic reform in China and

exchange rate adjustment.
That is now the direction of travel, but it doesn’t
address the underlying systemic issues.
Incidentally, those who believe the path of internal
demand is critical to rebalancing and that exchange
rate moves are secondary need to explain how an
acceleration in domestic demand would, on its own,

### Page 13

13
lead China’s external accounts to adjust. One
important, stylized fact about China is that domestic
demand growth is no longer feeding over to import
growth (ex-gold, that is).
Bottom line: China, which needs a 1.5 percentage
point contribution from net exports every year, is on a
collision course with its trading partners without a
currency correction that provides the basis for more
balanced trade even in the absence of trade
restrictions.
And there isn’t a realistic path towards balance that

doesn’t involve a stronger RMB; there aren’t, as Paul
Krugman once put it, immaculate transfers.
* That downturn shows up in domestic deflationary
pressure, and weak job growth/high rates of (at least
youth) unemployment. China, in other words, isn’t in
“internal balance.” I really liked the report from

### Page 14

14
Kamakshya Trivedi and Hui Shan of Goldman Sachs
arguing China needs two tools to hit two targets
(internal and external balance).
** To be sure, rate differentials matter for exporter
conversion—but so does the expected movement of
the RMB. The market understands this better than
the Fund. The Chen and Suwanapruti (Goldman
Sachs) note uses a framework similar to mine to
describe the CNY’s moves in Q3:
“In our view, sizeable FX inflows have continued to support

RMB appreciation despite unfavorable interest rate
differentials, as strong export receipts and increased exporter
FX conversions have outweighed portfolio outflows. Our
estimated FX conversion ratio rose to 63% in August,
compared with around 45% in normal years, likely reflecting a
shift in market expectations from RMB depreciation to
appreciation.”
*** Š ef č ovi č  has jurisdiction over trade policy
(narrowly defined), but not broader macroeconomic

policies. Europe’s institutional architecture for
exchange rate coordination is not well-developed.
**** The current account surplus is no longer masked
to the same extent as in 2023 and 2024, as SAFE has
fiddled with its BoP methodology once again (per the
Federal Reserve) and the BoP goods surplus is no
longer significantly below the customs goods surplus.
Of course, there are still problems in the data—the
deficit in the investment income account most

重點摘要 《經濟強勁帶來的高利率無損新興債利差穩步收斂 》
財政收支並非驅動新興主權信用利差的唯一因素 ，
總體經濟環境 、市場流動性均牽動利差走勢 ，因此
雖然自7月以來沙烏地阿拉伯等中東國家信用利差又
再擴大，但也大概在3年均值附近並不算高。以歷史
經驗來看，BB級主權國家利差通常對財政惡化程度
反應較大 ，可能是因為該評等僅低於投資等級一級 ，
財政變化容易牽動投資人對升等至投資級的預期與
投資部位的調整 ，而在投資等級的主權國家中 ，則
以匈牙利和波蘭這些債務負擔較重的主權債利差較
易受財政問題影響。
油價和利率是近期2項重要觀察變數，也牽動利差走
勢，不過由於新興主權債指數中約5成的組成為大宗
商品出口國、3成為石油出口國，反而能受惠油價上

漲，油價上漲時與利差走勢敏感度也較油價下跌時
低；然而 ，更重要的是高油價對通膨和政策應對的
二階影響 ，將導致高利率長時間延續的可能性並最
終衝擊實體經濟 ，進一步限制石油出口國利差收窄 。
以長期趨勢來看 ，利率水準的絕對值高低不必然影
響新興債利差 ，利率走勢反而和信用利差呈現小幅
負相關，利率走升反映的若是強勁經濟成長而非能
源供給衝擊 ，此時往往能伴隨信用利差收窄 ，反而
需留意的是利率波動放大及利率的大幅重新定價 ，
這才是牽動利差波動加大的主因 。目前總體經濟環
境部分或可與2004~2007年相比擬，當時在強勁成
長的背景下利率長時間在4%~5.3%高位震盪，但新
興主要貨幣主權債利差仍可收斂至 134點(此波低點
189點)，若經濟成長能在現今高油價和高利率環境
下持續強勁，利差則可望保持穩定。

重點摘要 《景氣及企業獲利續成長 ，企業債信改善趨勢延續 》
三大信評機構持續認可新興市場四大區域企業信用
評等的改善，3Q26新興市場企業債淨升等規模大幅
提高至760億美元，其中獲上調規模達到910億美元、
創下2025年第四季以來的最高水平 ，也已是連續第
5個季度改善。
3Q26新興市場4大區域評等調升數量均高於下調 ，
其中以亞洲改善動能最為顯著 ，主要貢獻來自於亞
洲金融業 ，全年升評 /降評比率已來到 1.8倍，逆轉
2019年降評多於升評的劣勢；拉美企業仍是新興市
場中違約率最高的區域 ，降評債券數量與其他區域
比也確實較高 ，但降評企業家數已是過去 10年來最
低，加上阿根廷主權債信獲上調帶動企業債 (主要是
國有企業)信評調升，拉美航空業者如南美航空集團

(LATAM Airlines)在油價維持高位環境下仍於3Q26
獲信評機構調升至 BB+，在企業債信分化環境下仍
有亮點 ，因此第三季拉美企業淨評級上調規模達
370億美元，反而創下2025年第三季以來的最佳季
度表現 ，全年共有 234家拉美企業信評得調升 。新
歐中東地區債信今年算是少數債信惡化的區域 ，很
大部分是受到戰爭及高油價影響所致 ，不過奈及利
亞和南非等主權評級上調仍帶來正向效果 ，梯瓦製
藥(Teva)評等更是上調至投資等級，帶來了120億美
元的貢獻，部分抵消地緣政治風險帶來的影響。
強勁的獲利成長持續支持新興企業穩健基本面 ，有
限的違約率輔以韌性十足的總經環境 、以及活躍但
不過度集中的初級市場 ，均是支持債信改善的原因 ，
預期在企業獲利仍看好的情境下 ，第四季企業債信
仍將朝正向發展。

重點摘要 《聯準會升息年 ，新興債雖有波動但正報酬機率高 》
觀察過往聯準會升息年度 ，利率溫和走升機率相對
較高，新興債市雖然多會受到升息壓力而出現一波
跌勢，但全年度仍有較大機率收紅 ，1996年以來僅
有2018、2022這兩個升息年度新興債市全年收黑 。
不過2022年新興債市重挫很大一部分原因來自於聯
準會在短短一年時間內將基準利率自0％升至4.25%，
這種猛爆性升息與目前所預設的風險管理式的溫和
升息環境有所不同；另外 ，2018年聯準會雖只升息
四碼，但土耳其及阿根廷因美元稀缺引發流動性風
險，這2國經常帳赤字占 GDP比重當時均高於 5%，
對外融資壓力上升的同時進而爆發金融危機 。然而
現階段新興國家經常帳已普遍改善 ，土耳其經常帳

赤字已降至 2%~3%，阿根廷更轉為順差 ，基本面
與2018年有很大的差異。若扣除這兩段期間，新興
債市在聯準會升息期間波動雖可能放大 ，但在貨幣
政策方向更趨明朗後 ，走勢便會止穩反彈 ，全年平
均報酬率仍有10%以上。
至於新興市場企業債部分 ，過去因升息所造成的跌
勢約是主權債的一半 ，主要是因為企業債發行天期
多較主權要來得短 ，加上該期間獲利動能強勁 ，因
此在利率上升時期表現往往相對主權債更具韌性 。
儘管利率走勢仍存不確定性，但最終若能穩定在5%
左右，預估新興企業債全年總報酬仍可維持在3%，
除非未來出現更大的外部衝擊 ，如利率持續大幅上
升引發對經濟成長受損的擔憂 ，或AI驅動的成長模
式被重新評價 ，否則對新興債市的看法仍將維持正
向，新興主要貨幣主權債在這樣的大環境下 ，短線
雖相對承壓，但後續反彈力道也可望大於企業債。
• 新興主要貨幣主權債在聯準

3Q26 營收大致符合預期，獲利優於預期 
欣興 3Q26 營收 526.5 億元(季增 22.8%/年增 54.9%)，營收達成率 99%，符
合預期，預期成長最明顯仍將為 ABF 及 HDI，兩者合計營收比重約 80%， 
ABF 及 HDI 嫁動率仍持續向上，毛利率因調整員工薪酬認列比率，於 3Q26
追朔此前的酬勞費用進行一次性認列，3Q26 毛利率為 28.8%，低於預估的
29.3%，業外方面，利息收入 16.3 億元、金融評價約 4954 萬，整體稅後獲
利 100.5 億元，季減 23.4%，年增 358.1%，EPS 6.32 元。 
光復 1 廠產能陸續開出，4Q26 估營收季增 14% 
展望 4Q26/1Q27，光復/楊梅廠高階 ABF 產能稼動率持續維持 90%以上，
隨美系客戶 GPU/CPU 產品量產及大尺寸高層數帶來的產品組合優化，載板
廠獲利已明顯提升，後續 ABF 毛利率預期逐季優化。另蘆竹 HDI 新設備於
1H26 進駐後陸續調整，將配合美系客戶出貨時程加大出貨量，光模塊相關
需求也正在放量。綜合上述，本中心維持 4Q26 估計，預估 4Q26 營收將季
增 14%，毛利率 31.9%，同時就本中心觀察，2027 年起隨 ABF 產能缺口延
續，價格循環將延續，並估計 1Q27 營收將季增 4.6%，毛利率 32.8%；
4Q26/1Q27 稅 後 獲 利 將 分 別 為 114.1 億元 /126.8 億元，分別季增
13.5%/9.4%，EPS 7.17/7.85 元。 
高階載板趨勢向上不變，2026/27 年營運動能強勁 
美系客戶 HDI 產品開始放量、ABF 持續漲價、光模塊進入量產階段並預期
2026/27 年皆擴產 40-50%，2027 展望維持正向，上調 2027 年營收 6%至
2946.8 億元，年增 52.6%，毛利率 37.5%，EPS 43.36 元。本中心認為欣
興仍具備高階製程能力，將維持其競爭優勢，並受惠於高階載板供需緊俏、
產品組合優化及新產能陸續開出，2026-2027 年營運成長明確。因此，本中
心上調 2 倍本益比至 30 倍，並以 2027 年預估 EPS 推得目標價 1,300 元，
維持買進評等。

產能規劃越來越明確，再度上調長交期設備採購訂單金額 
目前已見設備瓶頸最長可達 30 個月，載板對於後續擴產及長交期訂單顯示客戶對於產能預付款已
陸續到位。此前欣興已決議加大資本支出預算，將 2026 年資本支出由此前的 340 億元，追加 197
億元至 537 億元，上修幅度 57%，其中 85%將用於 ABF 產能擴充、15%用於廠房及其他部分。產
能方面包括光復 2、楊梅 2 廠建置，同時也規劃於 2026 年底至 2027 年初將動土楊梅 3 廠(將為策
略客戶特定世代產品做準備 )，另外對於長交期設備採購訂單金額自 2M26 起已三度上調，將再增
加約 509 億元，整體金額由 316 億元成長至 825 億元。用以提前預訂交期較長的設備，確保往後
的產能擴充順利，同時也顯示終端客戶對於產能需求強勁，預計 2027 年 ABF 產能有望年增 30-
40%。

平台 。 規 格方 面 ， 為滿 足 大型AI 晶 片與 多 晶粒 封 裝需 求 ， 載板 尺 寸 持續 朝100×100mm²、
120×120mm²以上發展，增建層數亦由既有規格逐步朝高層數結構升級，並同步提高線路密度及布
線複雜度。同時，大尺寸與高層數規格升級亦同步推升製程難度，並使高階材料及設備成為產能擴
充的主要瓶頸。  隨載板面積及疊層數增加，製程對翹曲控制、層間對位精度、熱膨脹係數（ CTE）
匹配及微細線路良率的要求顯著提高，進一步帶動 Low CTE 玻璃布、低翹曲材料及高精度製程設
備需求。其中，日東紡已規劃於 2026 至 2027 會計年度擴充高階 T-glass 產能，並推動部分高階玻

璃布於台灣在地化生產，不過就本中心 TPCA 訪查後觀察，現 2027 年 T-glass 皆已大致分配完畢，
上游缺料狀況仍持續緊俏。
展望欣興 2026～2027 年營運，預期 ABF 載板、HDI 及光模組相關業務將同步成長，帶動營收規
模擴大及獲利能力提升。其中，ABF 載板受惠 AI GPU 、ASIC 及高階伺服器需求持續攀升，供需
缺口逐步浮現，預期 2027 年將持續漲價，搭配高階產品比重提升及新產能陸續開出，有望進一步
改善整體毛利率。HDI 方面，隨美系客戶新產品進入放量階段，相關營收貢獻可望逐季增加，光模
組方面，受惠 AI 資料中心高速傳輸需求快速擴張，800G 及 1.6T 光模組滲透率持續提升，經供應
鏈訪查了解目前主要同業如臻鼎、華通皆已見加速，欣興相關產品亦已進入量產階段，預計 2026
及 2027 年相關產能均將擴充 40%～50%，有助擴大營收貢獻。整體而言，考量 ABF 供需持續緊
俏、HDI 新產品放量，以及光模組需求快速成長，加上產品組合優化與產能擴充效益逐步顯現，預

期欣興 2026～2027 年營收及毛利率均有望優於原先預期，故本中心上調 2026／2027 年營收及獲
利預估，以反映高階產品需求增溫與營運成長動能提升。
展望欣興 2026/2027 年各項主要業務，美系客戶 HDI 產品開始放量，同時光模塊也進入量產階段，
ABF 方 面 已 出 現 供 需 缺 口 ， 預 期1Q27 仍 將 持 續 漲 價 ， 因 此 整 體 毛 利 率 將 同 步 改 善 ， 目 前
ABF/HDI 狀況皆維持正向，且產能持續開出，預期欣興也將受惠光模組需求進一步翻倍成長等廠商
近期皆指出 2026/2027 年需求將翻倍成長，光模塊方面預期 2026/2027 年皆擴產 40-50%，預期
2027 年也將持續受惠，本中心估計 2026 年營收 1932 億元，年增 47.2%，並上調 2027 年營收
6%至 2946.8 億元，年增 52.6%，毛利率 26.8%/37.5%，營業利益 341.7 億元/855.9 億元，年增
412%/150.5%，稅後獲利 396.2 億元/690 億元，年增 394.7%/74.1%，EPS 25.22/43.36 元。

產業概況  
AI 需求增溫造成 T-glass 玻纖布供應吃緊，助益近期 BT 載板報價調整 
低熱膨脹係數（Low CTE ）玻璃纖維布，簡稱 T-glass，為高階 AI ABF 載板及高階 BT 載板重要原
料，由 Nittobo(日東紡)獨家供應，並由日系廠商 Resonac(ABF 載板 CCL 主要供應商)、三菱瓦斯
(BT 載板 CCL 主要供應商)採用。由於高階 AI 晶片需求增溫帶動高階 AI ABF 載板出貨成長，造成
T-glass 供應吃緊並連帶使高階 BT 載板 CCL(終端用途包含記憶體控制器、手機 Ap、Sip 等)交貨
期拉長，T-glass 玻纖布供應正常時高階 BT 載板 CCL 交貨期約 8-10 週，後因供應吃緊造成交貨期
拉長至 16-20 週，目前因玻纖布供應更為緊張已無告知交貨期。 
經供應鏈調查，台系載板廠已於 2025 年 7 月開始針對部分採用 T-glass 之 BT 載板產品調漲價格，
此外 BT 載板亦有載板廠進行價格調漲，以反應高階玻纖布供應日漸緊缺，以及年初以來銅價、金
價等原物料成本上漲壓力。由於 BT 載板產業長期以來供過於求，且當前高階 AI 晶片普遍採用
ABF 載板，多數載板廠此前 BT 業務毛利率較為偏低，淡季時季毛利率多有承壓。本中心認為漲價
趨勢可延續，將有助載板廠獲利改善。

受惠 AI 發展浪潮帶動 AI GPU 、AI ASIC 等 AI 晶片需求成長，AI ABF 載板需求正向。本中心推測
短期高階 AI ABF 載板因獲利水準足夠暫無調漲壓力，但中長期隨需求持續上升、載板面積增大、
T-glass 供應持續吃緊，AI ABF 載板產品台系廠商後續仍有進一步議價空間。目前欣興、南電、景

則有望成為美系 AI GPU 載板第三供。此外部分載板廠因原物料上漲等成本壓力在 2Q25、3Q25 小
幅調整中低階 ABF 載板報價，本中心判斷若 T-glass 供應持續吃緊並排擠 E-glass 產能，則後續中
低階 ABF 載板價格有望進一步提升。

AI、ASIC、通用型強勢出擊，2026 年美系 CSP 資本支出估年增 91%  
在 ChatGPT 等 AI 應用陸續推向市場，各大業者紛紛開始研發自有超級大模型，包括 Gemini 
(Google)、Claude (Anthropic) 、Llama (Meta) 等，各大品牌開始大舉投入大型語言模型(LLM)市場，
且每一個產品的智慧皆持續提高，部分消費者也陸續從 ChatGPT 陣營轉移至 Gemini 陣營，反映
出消費者開始逐漸提升對 AI 的黏著度。根據 Grand View Research 調查，2024 年全球 AI 市場營
收約 2,792 億美元，預估 2030 年市場規模超過 3 兆美元，擁有超過 30% 的年複合增長率。 
面對這爆發性的長期成長趨勢，CSP 業者(Amazon、Microsoft、Google、Meta)在法說會上一致強
調，AI 投資已轉變為一項橫跨 2026 年的結構性戰略，CSP 大廠不僅持續擴大對 GB300 等次世代
AI 伺服器的採購，更將重點放在資料中心基礎設施的長期戰略規劃，以應對 AI 運算對電力及散熱
系統強勁成長的需求，確保未來數年內擁有足夠的能源與容量來支持持續迭代的大模型部署。本中
心認為，2026 年美國四大 CSP 資本支出將年增 91%，且將有一半的成長來自於資料中心建置，代
表了資料中心的不足及未來伺服器需求。明年不僅僅是 NVIDIA GB300 的天下，AWS、Google、
Meta ASIC 的崛起也將是一大關鍵，其中又以 Google TPU 需求最為強勁，已經有兩個客戶預計將
採購 TPU。 
另外，受惠於 AI 訓練與推論需求爆發的連帶效應，本中心預估 2026 年通用型伺服器出貨量將年增
23%，其中以存儲型伺服器需求最為強勁。隨著生成式 AI 應用普及和使用者數量暴增，CSP 等業
者必須不斷擴充容量，且不僅限於高階 GPU 伺服器，龐大的 AI 模型訓練和推論在使用狀態中將消
耗大量的數據(DATA)，使得存儲型伺服器的需求大增。

ASIC 進入高速成長期，GPU 需求仍維持擴張 
從 AI 晶片預期出貨來看，GPU 與 ASIC 需求均持續成長，但 2026 年後 ASIC 成長動能明顯加速。
Nvidia GPU 出貨量預估由 2025 年 565.7 萬顆增至 2026 年 650 萬顆、2027 年 850 萬顆，NVIDIA
加 AMD GPU 預估年增 17%及 34%；AMD 亦由 2025 年 90 萬顆增至 2027 年 180 萬顆，顯示通用
GPU 算力需求仍維持成長。 
相較之下，ASIC 受惠 CSP 加速自研晶片及導入規模擴大，總出貨量預估由 2025 年 380 萬顆大幅
增至 2026 年 725 萬顆、2027 年 1,360 萬顆，年增率達 91%及 88%，成長速度明顯高於 GPU。其
中 Google 仍為最大 ASIC 使用者， 2027 年用量預估達 800 萬顆，AWS 亦增至 320 萬顆，
Microsoft 及 Meta 同步擴大部署。我們認為，在資料中心電力逐漸成為算力擴張瓶頸下， CSP 將
更重視每瓦運算效能及整體運算成本， ASIC 針對特定運算工作的效率優勢有望推升滲透率，惟
GPU 憑藉通用性及軟體生態系優勢，仍將維持重要地位。

AI 晶片面積持續擴大，將使 ABF 載板用量大增 
隨著大型語言模型與生成式 AI 的算力需求快速攀升，AI 晶片的設計持續朝向更高運算密度與更大
面積發展。無論是 NVIDIA、AMD 或各家大廠的新世代加速器，都呈現晶粒尺寸擴大、功耗上升、
I/O 腳位數倍增的趨勢。在此背景下，ABF 載板的需求不僅以「量」擴張，更以「規格」升級為主
軸。為支撐大型 GPU/AI ASIC 的高頻寬連接與多晶片架構，ABF 層數、線寬線距、孔徑控制及翹
曲管理均需同步提升，帶動高端載板技術門檻不斷拉高。由於先進 AI 晶片的封裝面積更大、電源
與訊號整合更複雜，單顆晶片所需 ABF 載板面積與材料用量明顯增加。整體而言，AI 晶片規模擴
大正驅動 ABF 產業進入新一輪升級周期，高階需求將成為未來成長的主要動能。

ESG 分析  
分別藉由「在 ESG 議題上的曝險」和「個別公司在 ESG 議題上的執行力」兩個面向來衡量公司於 ESG 上的表現。 
► ESG 總分： 欣興電子整體的 ESG 風險評級屬於中等風險，於 Sustainalytics 資料庫所覆蓋的公司中排名亦排行於略為
領先的位置，在電子零組件行業的公司中排名略微領先同業。 
► 在 ESG 議題上的曝險： 欣興電子的整體曝險屬於中等水準，略為落後電子零組件行業的平均水準。公司較需要改善的  
ESG 議題包含營運方面的碳排、公司在生產中使用原材料的效率(不包括能源和石油產品)、人力資源等。 
► 個別公司在 ESG 議題上的執行力：欣興電子在針對重大 ESG 議題的管理水準和執行力屬中等。公司訊息揭露能力非常
優良，提供投資人及市場充足的資訊。由於在公司治理方面的結構，欣興的風險評級屬於中等。

賣出：根據本中心對該檔個股投資期間絕對或相對報酬率之預測，我們對該股持負面觀點。此一觀點係基於本中心對該股之發展前景、財務表現、利多題
材、評價資訊以及風險概況之分析。建議投資人於投資部位中減持該股。 
評估中：本中心之預估、評等、目標價尚在評估中，但仍積極追蹤該個股。 
限制評等：為遵循相關法令規章及/或元大之政策，暫不給予評等及目標價。

註：元大給予個股之目標價係依 12 個月投資期間計算。大中華探索系列報告並無正式之 12 個月目標價，其投資建議乃根據分析師報告中之指定期間分析
而得。

本周热点评论 
1、 菲央行加息 50 个基点，比索再创新低 
10 月 22 日， 菲律宾央行将目标逆回购利率上调50 个基点至 5.50%，
隔夜存款与贷款便利利率分别调整至 5.00%和 6.00%。 这是该行年内第
四次连续加息，也是 2023 年 2 月以来首次单次上调 50 个基点，幅度
超出市场普遍预期。 菲律宾9 月通胀由 8 月的 6.1%升至 7.2%， 核心通
胀升至 4.7%的三年高位，前 9 个月均值 5.4%，明显高于 2%至 4%的
目标区间。 中东冲突推高国际油价、 交通费用上调， 叠加厄尔尼诺对农
业产量的威胁， 构成本轮通胀的主要上行风险。 央行维持2026 年通胀
预测 6.1%不变，将 2027 年预测由 5.4%上调至 6.0%，预计 2028 年回
落至 3.3%。同期比索 10 月 20 日收于 63.361 的历史新低，22 日进一
步贬至 63.52，输入型通胀压力随之放大。 
中诚信国际点评： 
菲律宾央行此次加息反映出外部冲击、汇率贬值与国内增长放缓
之间的矛盾进一步加剧。能源价格上涨与比索走弱推高输入性通胀，
但国内投资疲弱限制了经济对外部冲击的消化能力，货币紧缩难以从
根本上缓解供给压力，反而可能进一步制约经济修复。 菲律宾本轮通
胀压力不仅来自国际能源及食品价格上涨，也受到比索贬值的放大。
由于菲律宾高度依赖能源进口，外部价格冲击将直接推高进口成本，
并通过运输、生产等环节向国内物价传导；经常账户赤字扩大也增加
了经济对外部融资环境的敏感度。央行加息有助于抑制通胀的二次传
导、稳定市场预期，但难以直接缓解能源 和食品供给冲击，汇率能否
企稳仍取决于外部环境及市场信心。与此同时，菲律宾经济增长放缓
不仅受到高通胀挤压居民实际购买力的影响， 也与公共建设投资收缩、
私人投资信心不足有关。加息可能进一步抬高融资成本，但若投资和
生产活动持续疲弱， 单纯依靠需求收缩难以改善供给约束。 财政方面，
菲律宾 2027 年赤字率目标已放宽至 GDP 的 5.1%， 而公共投资恢复不
足既拖累短期经济活动，也可能削弱中期增长潜力和税收基础；若通
过压缩投资控制赤字，又可能延缓经济修复，增加财政整固难度。后
续关键在于外部价格压力能否缓解，以及公共投资和私人投资能 否逐
步恢复。若输入性通胀持续、国内投资修复仍然滞后，菲律宾将面临
汇率与物价压力延续、增长动力不足及财政整固受阻的多重约束。

大利、西班牙和希腊相对德国的利差亦有所上升。

10 月 24 日， 法国多地再次爆发反生活费高涨示威， 部分示威者与

国多个城市的游行大致和平进行，但部分激进分子向警方投掷物品、
发射烟火，暴力程度较高；两名重伤者分别出现在图卢兹和克莱蒙费
朗。 此前一周的全国示威曾演变成严重街头暴力， 数百家商店遭抢掠，
共有 2700 人被捕；本轮示威同期被捕人数已高于前一周的 385 人，但
商店破坏及抢掠规模有所缩小，购物中心获得更严密保护。

警民冲突。 努涅斯称， 数千名激进分子聚集在队伍后方， 其中约500 人
被认定为暴力滋事者。 他表示， 警方加强部署、 加快应对、 扩大示威前
检查并强化商家防护，有助于改善整体情况，当局将在 10 月 24 日晚
至 25 日继续保持高度戒备。

款 
国际货币基金组织 （IMF） 已就巴基斯坦两项贷款安排的最新审查
与巴方达成工作人员级协议协议（staff-level agreement）。待国际货币
基金组织执行董事会批准后，巴基斯坦将可获得约 12.1 亿美元资金。
协议涵盖 70 亿美元扩展基金安排（EFF）第四次审查，以及韧性与可
持续性融资机制 （RSF） 第三次审查。 其中， 扩展基金安排下拟拨付约
10 亿美元，韧性与可持续性融资机制下拟拨付约 2.1 亿美元；两项安
排累计拨款规模将增至约 57 亿美元。 国际货币基金组织表示， 巴基斯
坦需继续推进财政整固和结构性改革，包括提高税收征管效能、实施
电子发票制度和风险导向税务稽查、优化公共支出及政府采购管理、
适时调整能源价格以防止循环债务再度累积。

周度观点及策略

### Page 4

周度观点
• 2026年前三季度国内生产总值达1071071亿元，按不变价同比增长4.6%。三次产业结构延续“三产主导”的特征，第三产业
增加值628255亿元、增速5.2%，对经济增长贡献率 66.3%，较上年同期抬升 5.6个百分点，是拉动增长的核心引擎；第一 、
二产业分别增长3.7%、3.8%，贡献率为4.6%和29.1%，三次产业占比依次为5.5%、35.8%、58.7%，产业结构持续向服务型经
济倾斜。
• 分季度来看，三季度GDP同比增速4.5%，较二季度回升0.2个百分点，高于市场预期的 4.4%。内部结构和前三季度趋势一致 ，
第三产业同样保持 5.2%的较快增速，贡献率66.5%，较上年同期提升 4.7个百分点，二产、一产增速则相对偏弱 。季节调整
后的环比数据进一步印证回暖信号 ，三季度GDP环比增长1.2%，环比增幅较二季度上行 0.3个百分点，显示经济内生动能边
际改善，整体运行保持平稳修复态势。
• 9月规模以上工业增加值同比实际增长5.5%，较上月加快0.3个百分点，环比增长0.61%，工业生产边际有所抬升。结构上制

造业是主要支撑 ，当月同比增速为 6.0%，显著高于采矿业的 1.3%；分主体来看股份制企业表现更强 ，增长6.0%，国有控股、
外资及港澳台资、私营企业增速相对偏低。
• 行业层面呈现明显分化 ，高端装备、电子制造亮眼，专用设备、铁路船舶航空航天设备 、计算机通信电子设备制造业分别
增长12.1%、11.7%、16.4%，而高耗能传统行业偏弱，非金属制品、有色冶炼、煤炭开采等行业同比回落。
• 工业品产量同样冷热不均，传统建材、粗钢、原油加工、整体汽车产量承压下行，但新能源汽车延续高增，当月产量187.0
万辆，增长16.9%，十种有色金属小幅持平、乙烯保持正增长。
• 1—9月社会消费品零售总额 370001亿元，同比增长1.1%，好于市场预期 。剔除汽车之后的零售增速抬升至 2.8%，反映汽车
板块对整体消费形成明显拖累。9月单月社零总额42433亿元，同比同样增长1.1%，剔除汽车后增速回升至3.9%。

### Page 5

周度观点
• 从消费形态来看，餐饮消费韧性持续优于商品零售，1—9月餐饮收入同比增长2.4%，高于商品零售1.0%的增速，9月餐饮收
入增速2.1%，也略高于商品零售1.0%，服务类消费相对更有支撑 ，商品端整体修复节奏偏缓 ，消费复苏呈现结构性分化特
征。
• 2026年1-9月全国固定资产投资（不含农户）完成334115亿元，可比口径同比下降7.2%，投资整体仍处承压状态。分产业看，
一、二、三产投资均同比回落，第三产业投资降幅达10.0%，是拖累整体投资的主要因素；工业投资整体 下降2.8%，内部出
现分化，采矿业投资增长3.2%，制造业、电力热力燃气及水供应业投资分别下降2.1%和6.8%。
• 基础设施投资同比下降4.2%，但新基建相关领域表现亮眼，信息传输业投资大幅增长30.8%，航空、水上运输业投资也保持
两位数增长。区域与市场主体层面投资普遍走弱，东、中、西、东北四大区域投资全部同比下滑，东北地区降幅达到26.0%，
区域分化较为突出。内资、港澳台资、外商企业投资均为负增长，民间固定资产投资同比下降10.4%，民间资本投资意愿偏

弱，成为当前投资端的主要压力点，仅部分高技术、新型基础设施细分领域形成结构性支撑。
• 2026年1-9月全国房地产开发 投资53364亿元，同比下降20.6%，住宅投资同步 下滑20.5%，地产开发端延续下行趋势 。房企
施工、新开工、竣工指标全线走弱，房屋施工面积同比下降12.8%，新开工面积下降24.9%，竣工面积下降25.1%，住宅相关
分项跌幅更深，反映房企生产经营偏谨慎，以销定产特征突出。
• 销售端呈现新房、二手房明显分化，1-9月新建商品房销售面积、销售额分别同比下降13.2%、13.9%，住宅销售同步回落；
但二手房交易网签面积61746万平方米，同比增长10.7%，存量房交易成为市场成交的重要支撑 。9月末新建商品房待售面积
同比小幅下降1.5%，其中待售3年以下面积降幅达到5.0%，短期库存去化取得一定成效。

### Page 18

工业企业利润总额
图：工业企业利润总额累计同比 图：工业企业利润总额当月值（手工计算）
资料来源：WIND、华联期货研究所 资料来源：WIND、华联期货研究所
1—8月份，全国规模以上工业企业实现利润总额 52719.8亿元，同比增长 15.7%（前值17.6%）。采矿业实现利润总额 7661.5亿元，同比增长 35.1%；制造业实现利润总额
39695.3亿元，增长17.4%；电力、热力、燃气及水生产和供应业实现利润总额5363.0亿元，下降12.0%。
主要行业利润情况如下：计算机、通信和其他电子设备制造业利润同比增长1.1倍，有色金属冶炼和压延加工业增长82.9%，煤炭开采和洗选业增长51.6%，化学原料和化学制
品制造业增长51.0%，石油和天然气开采业增长17.0%，纺织业增长11.9%，专用设备制造业下降2.1%，电气机械和器材制造业下降5.2%，电力、热力生产和供应业下降15.1%
，汽车制造业下降16.0%，农副食品加工业下降17.4%，非金属矿物制品业下降46.7%，黑色金属冶炼和压延加工业下降62.4%，石油、煤炭及其他燃料加工业由亏转盈。

2026年9月份，全国居民消费价格同比上涨0.9%。其中，食品价格下降1.7%，非食品价格上涨1.5%；消费品价格上涨1.0%，服务价格上涨0.8%。1—9月平均，全国居民消费价
格比上年同期上涨0.9%。
9月份，食品烟酒及在外餐饮类价格同比下降0.9%，影响CPI（居民消费价格指数）下降约0.26个百分点。食品中，鲜菜价格下降8.1%，影响CPI下降约0.14个百分点；畜肉类
价格下降3.7%，影响CPI下降约0.15个百分点，其中猪肉价格下降10.0%；蛋类价格上涨14.3%，影响CPI上涨约0.07个百分点。其他七大类价格同比六涨一降。其中，其他用
品及服务、交通通信、医疗保健价格分别上涨5.9%、4.3%和2.7%，教育文化娱乐、衣着、生活用品及服务价格分别上涨1.4%、1.2%和0.2%；居住价格下降0.3%。

价格下降0.6%，耐用消费品价格上涨1.6%。

海关总署披露数据显示，按美元计价，2026年9月我国出口4471.8亿美元，同比增长36.3%，增速较8月增加11.3个百分点，外贸表现强劲；进口同比增速回升 2.8个百分点至

31%。
从大类看，机电产品依然是出口的基本盘 ，当月出口近2984亿美元，1-9月累计同比增长29.0%，稳居第一大出口品类；而高新技术产品累计同比增长 45.6%，远超整体出口
21.3%的增速，出口结构正加速向高技术含量、高附加值方向升级。其中，集成电路累计同比增速飙升至108.1%（人民币口径），反映全球半导体景气度较高。传统劳动密集
型产品和部分周期品出口明显承压。家具及其零件累计同比仅增长2.2%，钢材累计同比转为-0.8%的负增长，既显示出海外地产链需求的疲软，也反映出部分产能过剩行业面
临的出口压力。

### Page 42

固定资产投资

### Page 43

固定资产投资额
图：三大产业固定资产累计投资额同比 图：建筑安装工程和设备工器具购置累计投资额同比
资料来源：WIND、华联期货研究所 资料来源：WIND、华联期货研究所
2026年1—9月份，全国固定资产投资 （不含农户 ）334115亿元，同比下降7.2%。从环比看，9月份固定资产投资增长 0.07%。分产业看，第一产业投资 6527亿元，同比下降
3.9%；第二产业投资129743亿元，下降2.7%；第三产业投资197845亿元，下降10.0%。
工业投资同比下降2.8%。其中，采矿业投资增长3.2%，制造业投资下降2.1%，电力、热力、燃气及水生产和供应业投资下降 6.8%。基础设施投资同比下降4.2%。其中，信息
传输业投资增长30.8%，航空运输业投资增长13.8%，水上运输业投资增长13.5%。

房地产开发施工
图：房地产开发投资累计同比走势 图：房屋施工面积累计同比走势
资料来源：WIND、华联期货研究所 资料来源：WIND、华联期货研究所
2026年1—9月份，全国房地产开发投资53364亿元，同比下降20.6%，降幅比1—8月份扩大0.7个百分点；其中，住宅投资41125亿元，下降20.5%，降幅扩大0.8个百分点。
2026年1—9月份房地产开发企业房屋施工面积565221万平方米，同比下降12.8%，降幅较上月持平；其中，住宅施工面积392558万平方米，下降13.2%。

### Page 84

中国制造业PMI
图：中国制造业PMI热力图
资料来源：WIND、华联期货研究所
2026年9月份，制造业采购经理指数（PMI）为50.1%，比上月增长0.3个百分点，升至扩张区间。
从分类指数看，构成制造业PMI的5个分类指数中，生产指数、新订单指数和供应商配送时间指数均高于临界点；原材料库存指数、从业人员指数低于临界点。生产指数为51.7%
，比上月上升1.3个百分点，表明制造业生产活动扩张加快。新订单指数为50.5%，比上月下降0.1个百分点，高于临界点，表明制造业市场需求继续改善。
高技术制造业PMI为52.5%，装备制造业为51.0%，持续位于扩张区间，相关行业保持较快增长，制造业结构优化升级态势明显；消费品行业和高耗能行业 PMI分别为50.7%和48%
，比上月上升1.7个和0.1个百分点，景气水平均有所回升。制造业21个调查行业中有12个高于临界点，较上月增加4个，行业景气度有所扩散。

价格指数双双回升。受近期原油、有色金属价格上行等因素影响，制造主要原材料购进价格指数为 60.8%，出厂价格指数为54.0%，比上月分别上升4.2个和3.6个百分点，均连
续两个月回升。价格回暖有望带动企业盈利边际改善，但原材料购进价格指数升幅大于出厂价格指数，中下游行业利润空间仍面临挤压。

摘要：
10 ⽉ 29 ⽇，⼯⾏、建⾏ A 股市值双双刷新上市以来⾼点，收盘价为 8.78 元、 12.04 元，当⽇涨幅
为 2.57% 、 2.29% 。
两家⼤⾏再创新⾼，延续了近期国有⼤⾏历史纪录密集刷新的⾛势。
华尔街⻅闻统计发现，截⾄ 29 ⽇，六⼤⾏年内累计 61 次刷新 A 股市值⾼点。
银⾏板块的强势，在当天的市场调整中尤为突出。
截⾄收盘，申万银⾏指数上涨 1.97% ，上证指数下跌 0.82% ，创业板指、科创 50 下跌 4.45% 、
4.27% 。四⼤⾏ A+H 合计市值升⾄约 10.03 万亿元，年内⾸次站上 10 万亿元⼤关。
⼤⾏市值持续攀升，恰逢中期分红陆续落地、业绩企稳回升和资本补充推进。稳定派息带来当
期回报，经营改善则为持续分红增添底⽓，让⼤⾏在市场波动中更具吸引⼒。
⾼点密集刷新
三季度以来，市场波动加⼤，稳定回报受到更多关注。随着⼤⾏盈利改善、中期分红陆续落

地，银⾏板块表现相对稳健。
华尔街⻅闻统计发现，进⼊ 10 ⽉，国有⼤⾏刷新历史纪录的节奏明显加快。
截⾄ 10 ⽉ 29 ⽇，六⼤⾏当⽉共计刷新 A 股市值⾼点 31 次，年内共计 61 次；其中，建⾏刷新纪录
最为频繁、达 27 次，中⾏、⼯⾏、交⾏分别为 15 次、 12 次、 7 次。
农⾏和邮储虽尚未刷新历史纪录， A 股市值也已达到年内最⾼位。
值得注意的是，农⾏与邮储年内相对温和的涨幅，需要放在去年已经⾛出⼀轮强势⾏情的背景
下观察，例如，农⾏ 2025 年 10 ⽉曾连续 13 个交易⽇上涨，彼时年内涨幅已超过 50% 。
截⾄ 10 ⽉ 29 ⽇，建⾏、中⾏、交⾏、⼯⾏、邮储、农⾏年内 A 股市值累计涨幅为 32.3% 、
27.6% 、 21.1% 、 15.4% 、 9.9% 、 2.1% 。

### Page 2

⼤⾏的强势，也是银⾏板块今年逆势⾛强的缩影。
截⾄ 10 ⽉ 29 ⽇，申万银⾏指数年内上涨 2.79% ，同期沪深 300 下跌 5.71% ，银⾏板块领先 8.50 个
百分点。
与这份相对收益相伴，银⾏股在机构组合中的分量也在增加。
中泰证券测算，三季度北向资⾦、被动基⾦和主动基⾦合计净流⼊银⾏板块约 649 亿元。主动基
⾦银⾏持仓⽐例由⼆季度的 1.10% 升⾄ 2.16% ，主动增配是⽐例上升的主要来源。
险资对⼤⾏的布局，则沿着举牌、增持持续推进。
平安⼈寿今年 1 ⽉披露，其持有的农⾏ H 股于去年 12 ⽉达到该⾏ H 股股本的 20% ，触发第四次举
牌；此前已于去年 2 ⽉、 5 ⽉和 8 ⽉三次举牌。
进⼊⼆季度，⼯⾏、中⾏、建⾏和邮储获得险资增持，六⼤⾏前⼗⼤流通股东中均有险资⾝
影。其中，中国⼈寿传统险账⼾继⼀季度增持⼯⾏后，⼆季度再增持 2355.86 万股。
盈利托底分红
⼤⾏吸引⻓期资⾦，稳定派息是重要原因。随着经营企稳回升，这份现⾦回报也有了更充⾜的
盈利⽀撑。

六⼤⾏ 2026 年中期分红⽐例均由 30% 提⾼⾄ 31% 左右。截⾄ 10 ⽉ 29 ⽇，建⾏、⼯⾏按近 12 个⽉
分红计算的股息率为 3.43% 、 3.74% 。

### Page 3

⻛险提⽰及免责条款
市场有⻛险，投资需谨慎。本⽂不构成个⼈投资建议，也未考虑到个别⽤⼾特殊的投资⽬标、财务状况或需要。⽤⼾应考虑本⽂
中的任何意⻅、观点或结论是否符合其特定状况。据此投资，责任⾃负。
在低利率环境下，持续派息契合险资等⻓期资⾦的配置需求。
分红⽐例提⾼的同时，⼤⾏的业绩增⻓也在稳定增加。
2026 年上半年，六⼤⾏营收、归⺟净利润同⽐增⻓ 9.38% 、 4.41% ，较 2025 年全年增速提⾼约
7.1 个、 2.8 个百分点；
六家均实现营收和净利润同⽐增⻓，经营回升的趋势进⼀步显现。
息差同样出现企稳信号。
⼆季度，国有⼤⾏净息差由⼀季度的 1.29% 回升⾄ 1.31% ，提⾼ 2 个基点。此前持续收窄的息差
开始⽌跌，为利息收⼊和盈利修复创造了条件。
与此同时，资本补充正在增强⼤⾏兼顾业务发展与股东回报的能⼒。
截⾄ 6 ⽉末，六⼤⾏核⼼⼀级资本充⾜率在 10.04% ⾄ 14.24% 之间。继 2025 年 5000 亿元特别国债
⽀持中⾏、建⾏、交⾏和邮储银⾏补充资本后，新⼀轮资本补充安排覆盖⼯⾏、农⾏。

今年安排的 3000 亿元特别国债⽤于⽀持 8 家中央⾦融企业补充核⼼⼀级资本，⾸期 1500 亿元已
于 10 ⽉完成招标。⼯⾏、农⾏拟通过定增合计募资不超过 2600 亿元，进⼀步增厚资本基础。
国信证券在四季度策略中指出，盈利企稳夯实分红基础，信贷增速放缓则有望减轻资本消耗压
⼒。资本补充、盈利增⻓与资本消耗放缓，共同影响⼤⾏在满⾜经营要求后⽤于股东回报的空
间。
这轮变化还延伸⾄银⾏业的经营环境，并开始反映在信⽤评级中。
10 ⽉ 27 ⽇，惠誉将中国银⾏业经营环境评分由 “bbb-” 上调⾄ “bbb” ，并将六⼤⾏⽣存⼒评级均上
调⼀个⼦级。这项评级主要衡量银⾏独⽴经营和抵御⻛险的能⼒。
惠誉给出的依据包括影⼦银⾏⻛险收敛、信息透明度提⾼、信贷纪律加强和监管框架完善。⻛
险敞⼝更透明、信贷扩张更有约束，使银⾏更有条件识别⻛险、控制损失，也增强了评级机构
对其经营韧性的评价。
惠誉分析指出， 2026 年上半年中国银⾏业贷款增速为 5% ，低于 2024 ⾄ 2025 年的 7% 。更平稳的

扩张节奏，有助于稳定杠杆⽔平、控制⻛险积累。
从盈利和息差回升，到资本补充推进、经营环境改善，⼤⾏维持稳定回报的条件正在逐步增
强。当市场波动加⼤，这种由经营韧性⽀撑的分红能⼒，也成为资⾦持续关注⼤⾏的重要理
由。

 宏观观点

海外宏观周报：美联储或按兵不动

⚫ 核心观点 
上周美股 AI产业链调整延续，小盘股表现相对占优。上周标普
500指数下跌0.5%，纳斯达克100指数下跌0.8%，罗素2000指数上
涨 2.0%。近期科技和通信板块持续面临卖压，投资者对非AI科技公
司的关注有所增加。产业链内部也出现明显分化，软件相关股票相对
强势，而电力供应商、电网建设等此前受益于数据中心投资的板块承
压，回调压力从芯片和云服务商扩散至配套基础设施板块。 
美债延续反弹，风险资产调整对长端债券形成支撑。截至上周五，
10年期美债收益率约为5.00%，较前一周下降约7个基点。尽管中东
风险和能源价格仍推升通胀担忧，AI相关股票走弱、信用市场压力推
动资金增配国债。我们预计长债收益率仍将宽幅震荡，短期进一步下
行的空间有限。近期美债反弹受到科技股调整及避险需求的支撑，但
美国增长韧性仍对收益率构成约束。 
本周美联储将召开议息会议。我们预计，本次会议美联储将维持
利率不变，12月可能再加息一次，明年的政策方向则有望转向降息。
近期风险资产调整和 AI相关企业融资压力上升，为美联储观察此前
加息的效果提供了理由。展望明年，若能源冲击逐步减弱，高融资成
本对消费和投资的抑制作用进一步显现，美联储将获得降息空间，但
降息时点和幅度仍受通胀回落进程约束。

⚫ 风险提示： 
若中东局势紧张加剧，能源冲击持续，核心通胀进一步扩散，同
时美国经济继续走强，美联储可能更大幅度加息。

1 海外宏观事件与数据跟踪

上周中东局势持续紧张。随着以色列和美国选举临近，对大规模军事行动可
能恢复的担忧继续支撑油价。与此同时，周末仍有外交信号释放：伊朗外交部表
示，正通过中间方向美国传递信息，尚未关闭外交窗口。美国方面，特朗普拒绝
透露是否计划对伊朗发动攻击。双方在谈判条件上的分歧仍然明显，短期克制不
足以消除市场对冲突升级和能源运输中断的担忧。

美国企业活动保持较快扩张。10月标普全球综合PMI初值由9月的58.4降
至57.6。其中，制造业PMI由55.9升至56，高于市场预期的55.5；服务业PMI
由58.8降至57.9，略低于预期的58。制造业订单和生产保持强劲，服务业扩张
虽有所放缓，但招聘需求仍较旺盛。调查显示，订单积压和供应商交货延迟加重，
企业将成本转嫁给客户的能力有所增强。

美股AI产业链调整延续， 小盘股表现相对占优。 上周标普500指数下跌0.5%，
纳斯达克 100指数下跌 0.8%，罗素 2000指数上涨 2.0%。周初科技股一度反弹，
但 AI基础设施融资压力及地缘局势升级再次打击风险偏好，周四市场出现集中
减仓。近期科技和通信板块持续面临卖压，投资者对非 AI科技公司的关注有所
增加。产业链内部也出现明显分化，软件相关股票相对强势，而电力供应商、电
网建设等此前受益于数据中心投资的板块承压，回调压力从芯片和云服务商扩散
至配套基础设施板块。

美债延续反弹，风险资产调整对长端债券形成支撑。截至上周五，10年期美
债收益率约为5.00%，较前一周下降约7个基点。尽管中东风险和能源价格仍推
升通胀担忧，AI相关股票走弱、信用市场压力推动资金增配国债。

中邮证券有限责任公司于 2002年9月经中国证券监督管理委员会批准设立， 公司注册资本61.68亿元人民币，
是中国邮政集团有限公司绝对控股的证券类金融子公司，公司是中邮创业基金管理股份有限公司的第二大股东。 
公司经营范围包括:证券经纪，证券自营，证券投资咨询，证券资产管理，融资融券，证券投资基金销售，证券

司。

位的特色精品券商。

摘要：
礼来公司凭借旗下减重与糖尿病药物的强劲需求，交出⼀份远超华尔街预期的三季度成绩单，
并再度上调全年展望，进⼀步巩固其在全球 GLP-1 药物市场的领导地位。
公司第三季度营收达 244 亿美元，同⽐增⻓ 39% ，超出分析师平均预期的 225 亿美元；调整后每
股收益 7.48 美元，亦⼤幅⾼于预期的 5.59 美元。受此提振，礼来股价周四早盘上涨 3.7% ，年内
累计涨幅扩⼤⾄约 20% 。
礼来将全年营收指引上调⾄ 910 亿⾄ 920 亿美元，⾼于此前的 850 亿⾄ 870 亿美元区间，这是公司
今年以来第三次上调全年展望。与此同时，考虑到近期收购产⽣的相关费⽤，公司将调整后每

股收益指引⼩幅下调⾄ 35 ⾄ 36 美元。

### Page 2

Mounjaro 与 Zepbound 双轮驱动，贡献逾六成营收
三季度业绩的核⼼推动⼒来⾃两款 GLP-1 明星药物。糖尿病治疗药物 Mounjaro 实现营收 107.2
亿美元，同⽐增⻓ 65% ，超出市场预期的 99.5 亿美元；减重药物 Zepbound 营收 53.5 亿美元，较
上季度增⻓ 8.6% ，同样⾼于预期的 50.1 亿美元。两款产品合计占礼来总营收的⽐例⾼达 66% 。
Zepbound 的强劲表现部分受益于美国医疗保险政策的重⼤转变。⾃今年 7 ⽉ 1 ⽇起， Medicare ⾸
次将减重药物纳⼊覆盖范围，据礼来介绍，⽬前约有 50 万名患者正通过所谓的 "Bridge 项⽬ " 使⽤
Foundayo 或 Zepbound 。据杰富瑞分析师 Akash Tewari 本周早些时候在研报中估计，该项⽬有
望在年底前为礼来带来约 40 亿美元的收⼊贡献。
礼来全球市场总裁 Ilya Yuffa 上⽉在摩根⼠丹利全球医疗健康⼤会上表⽰， "Bridge 项⽬在
Medicare 中的推进，可能是提升药物可及性的最重要单⼀驱动因素。 "

尽管整体业绩亮眼，礼来的减重⼝服药 Foundayo 表现未达市场预期，成为本季度的⼀处软肋。
该药三季度营收为 1.84 亿美元，低于 FactSet 预期的 2.99 亿美元，仅略⾼于其上市⾸季（⼆季度）
录得的 9800 万美元。
分析⼈⼠指出， Foundayo ⾯临来⾃诺和诺德旗下减重⼝服药的竞争压⼒ —— 后者较 Foundayo
早数⽉进⼊市场，已占据⼀定先发优势。据杰富瑞数据，礼来⽬前在美国处⽅减重药市场的份
额约为 64% ，但减重⼝服药赛道的竞争格局尚未完全确⽴。
其他品类药物表现分化：⼼⾎管及糖尿病⼝服药 Jardiance 营收 15.8 亿美元，同⽐⼤增 65% ；乳
腺癌药物 Verzenio 营收 15.1 亿美元，符合预期；传统糖尿病药物 Trulicity 营收 9.04 亿美元，同⽐

下滑 14% ，延续萎缩趋势。
研发管线进展积极，监管获批消息密集
三季度内，礼来在监管层⾯取得多项进展。美国 FDA 批准 Mounjaro 新适应症，⽤于降低 2 型糖尿
病成⼈患者的⼼⾎管⻛险；同时批准了每周⼀次的基础胰岛素 Onswik 、乳腺癌联合疗法 Inluriyo
以及⽤于未经治疗慢性淋巴细胞⽩⾎病的 Jaypirca 扩展适应症。
研发管线⽅⾯，礼来披露了多项积极的临床数据：在⼀项三期头对头试验中， retatrutide 在 2 型
糖尿病成⼈患者中的疗效优于司美格鲁肽 2mg ； Ebglyss 在中重度⼿⾜特应性⽪炎的三期研究中
显⽰正⾯结果； EloraTZP 在肥胖合并 2 型糖尿病患者中的⼆期结果亦为阳性，公司计划于 2026
年四季度启动三期试验。
本季度研发费⽤为 42 亿美元，同⽐增⻓ 21% 。此外，公司因收购迷幻药开发商 AtaiBeckley 及疫
苗⽣物技术公司 Curevo ，计⼊了约 42 亿美元的在研项⽬研发摊销费⽤（ IPR&D ），这也是当季净

利润 65 亿美元低于近期季度⽔平的主要原因。

2026 年 10 月 30 日 全6 頁

米 GDP 前期比年率＋3.4％と加速 
2026 年7-9 月期米GDP：内需、特に設備投資が強い

ニューヨークリサーチセンター 研究員 藤原 翼

[要約] 
 2026 年 7-9 月期（以下、7-9 月期）の実質 GDP 成長率は前期比年率＋3.4％と 2026 年
4-6 月期（以下、4-6 月期）から加速し、市場予想（Bloomberg 調査：同＋3.2％）を上
回った。屋台骨の個人消費が堅調を維持し、設備投資もAI 関連投資を中心に好調だっ
た。その結果、米国経済の自律的な成長を反映する民間最終需要（個人消費、設備投
資、住宅投資の和）は同＋4.9％と2 四半期連続で加速し、2021 年4-6 月期以来の高い
伸びとなった。米国経済は内需中心に堅調だったといえる。 
 2026 年 10-12 月期も内需中心に底堅い結果を見込むが、下振れリスクはある。個人消
費については、貯蓄率の低下に見られるように家計の消費余力は 低下している可能性
がある。また、足元では FRB による利上げを背景に金融環境が引き締まりつつあり、
金利に敏感な内需項目を 中心に下押しするとみられる。なかでも、設備投資のけん引
役である AI 関連投資は、一部で債務の持続可能性が懸念され始めている。更なる金融
環境の引き締まりが必要以上にAI 関連投資や景気を抑制する可能性に注意を要する。

内需中心に堅調さを維持 
2026 年 7-9 月期（以下、7-9 月期）の実質 GDP 成長率は前期比年率＋3.4％と 2026 年 4-6 月
期（以下、4-6 月期）から加速し、市場予想（Bloomberg 調査：同＋3.2％）を上回った。 
7-9 月期の実質GDP を需要項目別に見ると、屋台骨の個人消費が前期比年率＋3.8％と4-6 月
期と同様に高い伸びとなった。また、設備投資は同＋12.7％と加速し、大幅な伸びとなった。
他方で住宅投資は同▲3.3％とマイナスに転じた。その結果、米国経済の自律的な成長を反映
する民間最終需要（個人消費、設備投資、住宅投資の和）は同＋4.9％と 2 四半期連続で加速
し、2021 年 4-6 月期以来の高い伸びとなった。米国経済は内需中心に堅調だったといえる。 
また、7-9 月期は民間在庫の前期比年率寄与度が＋1.61％pt と押し上げ要因となった。他方
で、純輸出は同▲3.32％pt と 4 四半期連続で押し下げ要因となった。純輸出の内訳を見ると、
輸出（前期比年率▲5.7％）が3 四半期ぶりにマイナスに転じ、輸入（同＋19.7％）は2 四半期
連続で加速した。輸入については、力強いAI 関連の設備投資需要を背景に、拡大基調となって
いる。最後に、政府支出は同＋5.3％とプラスに転じた。

先行きは金融環境の引き締まりによる内需の抑制に注意 
2026 年 7-9 月期の GDP 統計では、屋台骨の個人消費が堅調を維持し、設備投資もAI 関連投
資を中心に好調だった。その結果、米国経済の自律的な成長を示す民間最終需要は2021 年 4-6
月期以来の高い伸びとなり、内需中心に堅調だったといえる。 
2026 年 10-12 月期も内需中心に底堅さが継続すると見込むが、下振れリスクはある。個人消
費については、貯蓄率の低下に見られるように家計の消費余力は低下している可能性がある。
こうした中で、エネルギー価格の再上昇を背景にインフレが高止まりすれば、個人消費はペー
スダウンし得る。また、足元では FRB による利上げを背景に金融環境が引き締まりつつあり、
金利に敏感な内需項目を中心に下押しするとみられる。なかでも、設備投資のけん引役である
AI 関連投資は、一部で債務の持続可能性が懸念され始めている。更なる金融環境の引き締まり
が必要以上にAI 関連投資や景気を抑制する可能性に注意を要する。

環境：緯穎宣示「 2030 年達成全球 100% 再生能源使用、 2040 年邁向淨零排
放」，減碳目標已通過 SBTi 審核。 2025 年全球再生能源使用率達 80.90% ，
廢棄物回收利用率達 82.00% ，並透過冰水主機溫度優化、生產設備節能及
LED 照明汰換等措施，全年節電 630,678 度，相當於減少 298.74 公噸 CO ₂e
排放。此外，公司推動木箱及棧板循環使用， 2025 年減少約 2,565 公噸廢棄
物，創造約 6.7 億元經濟效益，並逐步導入內部碳定價機制，將減碳效益納
入投資決策。  
社會：緯穎重視人才培育、員工福利及社會參與，持續推動全球線上學習、
專業職能訓練及多元共融職場。 2025 年全球員工平均受訓時數達 34 小時，
間接人員平均約 50 小時，並透過職涯發展及員工溝通機制強化人才留任。
對外則積極投入產學合作、實習人才培育、社區關懷及環境保育， 2025 年
社會投入金額達 2,819 萬元，並透過緯穎永續基金會推動公益活動，累計投
入全球植樹 57,782 棵及珊瑚復育 8,296 株，持續擴大企業社會影響力。  
治理：  緯穎以董事會為公司治理最高機構，設有審計委員會、薪資報酬委
員會、提名委員會及企業永續發展委員會，定期檢視公司治理與永續發展績
效。公司將 ESG 績效納入高階經理人薪酬考核，並建立風險暨安全管理機
制，每年至少兩次向審計委員會及董事會報告。此外，依循責任商業聯盟
（ RBA ）準則落實誠信經營與反貪腐管理， 2025 年全球員工行為準則簽署
率及教育訓練涵蓋率均達 100% ，當年度未發生違反誠信道德或涉及貪腐之
情事。  
公司簡介  
緯穎科技（ 6669 TT ）成立於 2012 年，為緯創集團旗下專注於超大規模資料
中心（ Hyperscale Data Center ）及雲端基礎架構的伺服器設計與製造商， 2019
年於台灣證券交易所掛牌上市。公司主要提供雲端運算、人工智慧及資料中
心所需之伺服器、儲存設備、網路系統及機櫃基礎設施，並提供客製化產品
設計、系統整合及軟硬體解決方案。緯穎為開放運算計畫 （ OCP ） 白金會員，
主要採 ODM Direct 商業模式，直接服務全球大型雲端服務供應商（ CSP ），
產品涵蓋通用型伺服器、 AI GPU 伺服器及客製化 ASIC 伺服器，並提供 L6
主機板、 L10 整機及 L11 整櫃等不同層級的系統整合服務。公司以台灣為研
發及營運核心，於墨西哥、馬來西亞及美國等地布局生產與服務據點，主要
台灣同業競爭對手包括鴻海（ 2317 TT ）、廣達（ 2382 TT ）。 2023 年地區別
營收比重為：美洲 78.58% 、歐洲 11.90% 、亞洲 7.73% 、其他地區 1.21% 、
台灣內銷 0.57% ，顯示公司營收高度集中於美洲市場。  
3Q26 營收 QoQ+56.3% ，營運重心逐步轉向 ASIC ：  
緯穎 2Q26 營收 2,781.53 億元， QoQ+0.59% ；毛利率 9.26% ，QoQ+1.7ppts ；
營益率 7.27% ，毛利率季增主要受惠 2Q26 有部分專案轉為寄售制
(Consignment) 模式，加上新平台導入帶來較高 NRE 收入；稅後淨利 149.69
億元， YoY+23.5% 。 3Q26 營收  4,346.18 億元， QoQ+56.3% ，除 ASIC 持續
放量外，通用型的強勁需求亦帶動營收增長，管理層預估 3Q26 通用型與
ASIC 伺服器出貨比重接近各半， 4Q26 ASIC 比重將進一步增加， GPU 新平
台預計於 4Q26 開始出貨，然而放量時間點約落在 1H27 。 4Q26 營運重點仍
在於既有通用型需求延續與 ASIC 出貨成長， GPU 平台主要貢獻將反映於

3 群益投顧 
2027 年。  
通用型與 ASIC 提供營運支撐，預計 Trainium 3 液冷將於 2027 年放量 ：  
目前緯穎的成長基礎仍在通用型及 ASIC 伺服器 ，GPU 新平台則成為未來另
一重要成長引擎，但較高的 BOM 也將帶來毛利率稀釋效果。通用型、 ASIC
專案改採寄售模式將有助降低高價零組件對營收及銷貨成本的影響；此外，
ASIC 比重增加將使客製化系統設計與機櫃整合能力的重要性提高，兩者都
將有助於支撐毛利率。 2027 年 ASIC 業務的觀察重點包括 Trainium 3 液冷
平台以及新增 ASIC 專案的機會。目前緯穎為 Trainium 3 平台的主要供應
商，液冷的導入將增加機櫃散熱、供電與系統測試的整合需求，液冷版本除
ASP 將高於氣冷版本外，組裝上的難度提升也將提升緯穎的 value-added 。
未來觀察的重點除是否如期量產外，還須留意是否有其他 ASIC 專案改採寄
售制。  
Vera Rubin 與 Helios 擴大產品布局 ：  
緯穎於 10/2026 OCP 中表示其與緯創為 NVIDIA Vera Rubin NVL72 首批
Pilot Build Partners 之一，將參與驗證及 design-in ，同場展示的 AMD Helios
則採用 MI450 系列 GPU 機櫃，預期  4Q26 後段 GPU 新平台可小量出貨，
並於 1H27 放量。因此我們認為 2027 年 GPU 專案將有助於顯著提升營收規
模，但物料模式將影響營收及毛利率表現，若採買賣制 (Buy and Sell) ，零組
件金額會擴大營收與成本；若部分專案或高價物件採寄售制，將有助緯穎維
持毛利率。  
德州二廠預計 2Q27 投產，支援美國在地機櫃與液冷交付 ：  
美國產能擴充有助緯穎承接客戶在地製造需求。德州第一棟廠房約 39.3 萬
平方英尺， 2025 年底開始出貨，並已進入量產；第二棟約 47.6 萬平方英尺，
公司預計於  2Q27 開始生產。德州基地具備氣冷及液冷機櫃的生產、整合與
測試能力，搭配 Amazo 合作，將強化緯穎在美國的系統交付布局。管理層
目標為 2027 年美國廠約占整體組裝產能兩成，因此我們認為德州二廠主要
支援 2027 年後續擴張， 1H27 營運仍由既有據點及已投產的美國產線支應。
2026 年營收預估 YoY+61.2% ， ASIC 擴張帶動營收增長 ：  
群益預估  4Q26 營收 5,432.09 億元， QoQ+24.99% ；毛利率 8.59% ；營益率
7.01% ；稅後淨利 309.33 億元； EPS 55.34 元。 2026 全年營收 15,324.87 億
元， YoY+61.2% ；毛利率 8.63% ；營益率 6.99% ，營業利益 1,071.78 億元，
YoY+67.7% ；稅後淨利 856.54 億元， YoY+67.6% ； EPS 153.23 元。 ASIC 比
重提升及通用型強勁的需求是帶動營收成長的主要動能， GPU 系列平台則
預計將於 1H27 開始顯著貢獻營收。  
群益預估 2027 年營收 YoY+88.1% ：  
緯穎的成長動能包括既有通用型需求延續、 Trainuim 3 液冷專案、潛在的
ASIC 新專案機會，以及 GPU 新平台擴大營收貢獻，美國產能則支援在地交
付能力提升。預期 2Q27 受 Helios 平台及  Vera Rubin 相繼放量的影響下，
毛利率將自 1Q27 有較明顯的衰退，群益預估 2Q27 毛利率 7.80% ， QoQ-
0.7ppts 。預估 2027 全年營收 28,825.99 億元， YoY+88.1% ；營收大幅增長的
同時， AI 伺服器較高價的零組件將造成毛利率稀釋， 2027 年毛利率 7.83% ，

Source PDF: all report pdf/英伟达出手背书新兴云厂商：为Nscale逾50亿美元建设融资提供担保.pdf
Report source: WallstreetCN (Global)
Date: 2026-10-30
Pages: 2
Status: ok

### Page 1

英伟达正与 Nscale 洽谈，拟为其 460 兆⽡数据中⼼建设提供逾 50 亿美元信⽤担保，该设施
将服务于 Anthropic 。此次担保以剩余价值担保形式构建，若 Nscale 违约，英伟达将介⼊接
管设施。这是英伟达扶持新兴云⼚商⽣态系列动作的最新⼀例，其迄今已累计提供约 1700
亿美元信⽤⽀持与投资。
摘要：
英伟达正与新兴 AI 云服务商 Nscale 洽谈，拟为后者在美国西弗吉尼亚州建设 460 兆⽡数据中⼼的
债务提供数⼗亿美元信⽤担保。该数据中⼼将专⻔服务于 AI 公司 Anthropic，双⽅已签订 450 亿
美元的租⽤合同。
据 The Information 最新报道，此次担保⾦额预计逾 50 亿美元。若交易落地，将进⼀步强化英伟
达与 Anthropic 之间的芯⽚供应纽带 ——Anthropic 是全球最⼤ AI 服务器芯⽚⽤⼾之⼀，但其⼀贯
采取多元化芯⽚采购策略，并⾮完全依赖英伟达。
⽬前协议尚未签署，条款仍可能变动。
担保结构：剩余价值担保，⾮芯⽚或租约

据知情⼈⼠向媒体透露，此次担保将以 “ 剩余价值担保 ” 形式构建，担保对象是数据中⼼设施本
⾝，⽽⾮租约或芯⽚。
这⼀结构将使 Nscale 能够以投资级评级为项⽬建设融资。若 Nscale 未能按时⽀付建设款项，英
伟达将介⼊代为付款，并在过渡期内接管该设施，同时协助安排转售和转租事宜。
知情⼈⼠表⽰，这与英伟达此前更⼤规模的信⽤⽀持协议有所不同 —— 此前的协议通常覆盖客
⼾的数据中⼼租约或芯⽚融资，⽽此次直接针对电⼒与建设成本。
450 亿美元合同背后： Nscale 与 Anthropic 的西弗吉尼亚项⽬
Nscale 上⽉在 IPO 招股书中披露，已与 Anthropic 签订 450 亿美元合同，租⽤其位于西弗吉尼亚州
Monarch 数据中⼼园区⾸栋 460 兆⽡建筑。该设施将配备英伟达最新⼀代 Vera Rubin GPU 。
据⾏业估算，建设 1 吉⽡供电能⼒的数据中⼼外壳成本约为 120 亿美元，据此推算，英伟达为
Nscale 这⼀项⽬提供的信⽤⽀持规模很可能超过 50 亿美元。此前报道称，相关建设成本持续攀

升。
此外，据爆料， Anthropic 还计划租⽤该西弗吉尼亚园区的第⼆期设施，合同规模与第⼀期⼤致
相当。
英伟达的战略逻辑：绑定 Anthropic ，守住新兴云⽣态
⼀位⾏业投资者分析认为，英伟达此举的核⼼动机在于确保 Nscale 的成功，进⽽维系与
Anthropic 的深度绑定。
Anthropic 与多数同⾏不同，其芯⽚采购策略更为多元，并⾮主要依赖英伟达。英伟达若能通过
信⽤背书推动 Nscale 项⽬落地，实质上是在为⾃家 Vera Rubin 芯⽚锁定⼀个⼤规模应⽤场景。

芯⽚，以降低对英伟达的依赖。这使得 Nscale 、 CoreWeave 、 Firmus 等新兴云⼚商
（ neocloud ）对英伟达的战略价值愈发凸显。英伟达今年夏天甚⾄调整了营收披露⽅式，专⻔
突出新兴云⼚商的贡献 —— 这⼀群体⾃ 2023 年 GPU 需求爆发以来，已成为英伟达重点扶持的对
象。
1700 亿美元⽣态押注：英伟达的新兴云战略全貌
英伟达迄今已向新兴云⼚商及其他⼤型客⼾提供约 1700 亿美元的信⽤⽀持与投资。
除 Nscale 外，英伟达还在洽谈向澳⼤利亚 AI 云服务商 Firmus 投资数亿美元。 Firmus 本⽉初突然
撤回了 IPO 申请，据 The Information 上周报道，英伟达的潜在投资正是谈判背景之⼀。

为⽀撑这⼀⽣态，英伟达内部专⻔组建了⼀⽀团队，由⻩仁勋的⼥婿 Nico Caprez 联合领导，协
助新兴云⼚商寻找具备可⽤电⼒的数据中⼼选址 —— 这类资源极为稀缺，⽆论是⾃建独⽴电源
还是接⼊电⽹，均需耗费⼤量时间。
然⽽，新兴云⼚商普遍⾯临严峻的财务压⼒：这些公司⼤多尚未经过市场验证，需要⼤幅增⻓
营收才能偿还为购买英伟达服务器⽽举借的巨额债务，⽽利率的持续上升令这⼀压⼒进⼀步加
剧。业内部分⾼管认为，该⾏业的整合已是⼤势所趋。英伟达是否持续为这⼀⽣态提供⽀撑，
将直接决定部分新兴云⼚商的⽣死存亡。
